title: 特朗普威胁推进和解基金，给总检察长谈判带来新的不确定性
content:
总统唐纳德·特朗普周六威胁称，如果两名共和党顽固分子不支持他的司法部长提名人，他将推出一项基金来补偿他的盟友，这给计划于下周进行的参议院确认投票注入了新的不确定性，并再次强调了他有兴趣为那些感到不公正迫害的支持者获得报酬。

特朗普在他的《真相社会》帖子中声称，他将继续担任代理司法部长托德·布兰奇，并施压如果得克萨斯州参议员约翰·科宁和北卡罗来纳州参议员汤姆·蒂利斯拒绝支持前联邦检察官，那么他们将在“反武器化基金”上领先。在共和党与四项起诉书作斗争时，这位前联邦检察官是特朗普辩护团队的关键成员。

政府需要他们的选票，但两位议员都抗议布兰奇的选择，因为一项诉讼和解协议设立了一项 18 亿美元的基金，以补偿那些感到受到刑事司法系统虐待的人，并为特朗普及其家人提供豁免权税务审计。

周五，特朗普宣布该基金“死亡”，这是明显进展的迹象。随着谈判持续到深夜，参议院司法委员会主席、参议员查克·格拉斯利 (Chuck Grassley) 重新安排了本周早些时候推迟的对布兰奇的委员会投票。

该委员会的一位发言人表示，爱荷华州共和党人格拉斯利希望看到布兰奇在 8 月休会前得到确认，并将周二的投票列入日程“可以让白宫有更多时间确保为总统选举投票” ”

但到了周六早上，这些计划因特朗普的一项新声明而陷入危险，该声明似乎将基金重新摆上桌面，并打击了将在 1 月份任期结束时离开国会山的两位参议员。

“如果参议员科宁和蒂利斯因我不支持他们而感到不安（他们分别输掉了，并退出了！），他们不会批准托德·布兰奇，他是提名人之一。全国每个人都认为最受尊敬的专业人士成为美国司法部长，那么我将继续让托德担任代理总检察长，并努力推动“恢复该基金”。总统坚称，正如他之前所做的那样，该基金“照顾那些在民主党总统巴拉克·奥巴马和乔·拜登执政期间受到如此恶劣待遇的人”。

即将退休的蒂利斯注意到了总统的转变，他在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，尽管特朗普周五发表了评论，但他“显然打算通过不恰当地建立另一个虚假基金或推动国会投票通过一项法案来恢复对朋克的支付。参议院的大多数共和党人都会反对。”

他补充道：“不幸的是，我认为有资格担任这一职务的托德·布兰奇将不会因为这一逆转而得到确认。希望我们能在周二之前解决这个问题。”

布兰奇在两个月前的一次听证会上表示，在共和党参议员反抗并推迟移民资助后，反武器化基金将不会向前推进。

但今年在特朗普支持其主要对手后失去连任的蒂利斯和科宁表示，他们希望确保白宫不会改变方向，特别是在特朗普继续辩称需要一笔资金的情况下。

根据《The》审查的一份文件，司法部已向参议员提供了措辞，称布兰奇 5 月 18 日设立“反武器化基金”的命令已“撤销，且不具有任何效力”。美联社。

科宁和蒂利斯表示，他们还希望对和解协议的另一部分进行一些澄清，该部分将授予特朗普及其家庭成员免受税务审计的豁免权。科宁本周表示，据他了解，审计未来可能会扩大到 100 多家不同的特朗普集团子公司。

“托德·布兰奇表示，这仅限于诉讼各方，而且是追溯性的，而不是前瞻性的，”科宁说。 “我们所做的就是要求他们将其书面化。”

title: 伯克希尔哈撒韦公司股价创八个月新高
content:
(This is the Warren Buffett Watch newsletter, news and analysis on all things Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway. You can sign uphereto receive it every Friday evening in your inbox.)

Berkshire Hathaway shares rallied to an eight-month high this week and there could be more gains ahead if they continue to catch up to the S&P 500.

TheB sharesclosed Tuesday at $512.37, their highest level since November 28, when they finished at $513.81.

They closed Friday at $511.54, down 5.2% from the all-time closing high of $539.80 on May 2 of last year, the day beforeWarren Buffett revealed he would step down as CEOat the end 2025.

TheClass A sharesended Tuesday at $768,010, also their highest close since November 28's $770,100.

Friday's close of $766,600 was 5.3% below their all-time closing high of $809,350.

A story inBarron'ssaysBerkshire's rally "has room to run" since the stock remains "well behind" the benchmarkS&P 500, which is 7.6 percentage points ahead.

But Berkshire has erased more than half of its 17.5 percentage point deficit just two months ago.

Berkshire is also lagging behind competitors in two key sectors: railroads ...

Another positive for Berkshire is the big gains for three of its biggestequity portfolio holdings.

Number oneApple, now worth more than $70 billion, is up 13.6% so far this year.

Coca-Cola, Berkshire's third largest position at $35 billion, has jumped 25% year-to-date. Earnings this week came inahead of expectations and Coke raised its full-year outlook.

Number fourBank of Americais up 12.6% on the year. That stake is now valued at almost $32 billion.

Berkshire's gain of around 3% on Tuesday may have been partially fueled by UBS analyst Brian Meredithraising his price target on the B sharesto $585 from $570, and on the A shares to $877,848 from $854,596.

While maintaining a "buy" rating, Meredith also edged his earnings estimates higher and welcomedaBarron'sreporttwo weeks ago that Berkshire appeared to have bought back as much as $11 billion of its stock in the second quarter.

We'll get the actual number when Berkshire releases second-quarter results, expected on Saturday, August 8.

Some links may require a subscription:

Warren Buffett respondsto a request from an audience member to enlist the support of his "cousin" Jimmy Buffett in saving the trees in the Florida botanical garden and theme park Cypress Gardens.

AUDIENCE MEMBER: Several weeks from now I'll be before [Florida]Governor [Jeb] Bushwith the Friends of Cypress Gardens. We have a website ... trying to keep a developer from clear-cutting the trees in Cypress Gardens, a national treasure.

And my question is, would you consider contacting your "cousin," [musician]Jimmy Buffett, about possibly helping us in some way? ...

WARREN BUFFETT: I get asked to contact — probably the one I get asked to contact the most isBill Gates, but I get asked to contact all kinds of people.

And I mean, everybody is slipping me envelopes with letters in them, sending things to the office and saying, "Won't you get this person?" and all they can say is no.

I don't do — I don't make requests of my friends, basically, for anything.

And I just — I would spend the rest of my life doing it. They would feel — I would never know — (applause) — you know, what they were doing —

You know, I would never know what they were doing because I was asking versus what they really felt.

I mean it's an impossible — from my standpoint at least — that's an impossible game to get into, in terms of that.

I mean when [Washington Post publisher]Kay Grahamwas alive, everybody, you know, wanted her for one reason or another. And they've all got causes.

And, frankly, they, you know, they want to use me to get her, or Jimmy Buffett, or whomever, to say yes to something that they're saying yes to, partially, because they feel they don't want to say no to me.

And I, you know, that — I just don't want to use my friendship for that purpose, frankly.

And I don't do it, even for things that I strongly believe in, myself...

I've never had one of those honorary dinners where they send out, you know, to all the suppliers to Berkshire and everything and start leaning on them and saying, you know, "We're honoring Warren."

Well, hell, if they want to honor me, they can honor me without soliciting all my friends for money. I mean, I don't consider that much of an honor if the reason they picked me was because I got rich friends.

title: 特朗普媒体新的付费数据服务上线，让客户更快地访问特朗普的帖子
content:
特朗普媒体和技术集团于 8 月 1 日推出新的付费数据服务，可以更快地访问唐纳德·特朗普总统和平台上其他顶级帐户的 Truth Social 帖子。

新的应用程序编程接口“Truth API”旨在为企业提供“直接、经过许可、实时反馈该平台最具市场影响力的真相”，临时首席执行官 Kevin McGurn 在宣布该服务的新闻稿中表示。

虽然没有明确点名特朗普，但总统的@realDonaldTrump帐户是Truth Social上迄今为止最大的帐户，经常首先在那里发布他最重要的政策决定，包括与伊朗战争的最新消息。

截至周六，该帐户拥有1300万粉丝。

特朗普的家族也是运营Truth Social的上市公司特朗普媒体的最大股东。

该帐户是在民主党之后推出的。加州参议员亚当·希夫 (Adam Schiff) 和马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 将矛头指向了这项新服务，周三敦促美国证券交易委员会调查该公司是否违法。

他们在周二写给美国证券交易委员会 (SEC) 主席保罗·阿特金斯 (Paul Atkins) 的一封信中写道，“这似乎是为了个人利益而滥用总统职权，损害了普通投资者和我们市场的诚信，同时让华尔街和其他富有的内部人士致富”。

美国证券交易委员会 (SEC) 拒绝了这一要求。

“市场已经根据 Truth Social 的帖子发生变化，”Truth Media 的 McGurn 在宣布这一消息时写道。 “Truth API 提供了平台上最具市场影响力的真相的直接、许可、实时反馈，同时推进了我们通过高利润、经常性收入流将专有资产货币化的战略。”

title: 只看赔率是不够的。交易者如何在预测市场上获得优势
content:
It's been less than a year since 26-year-old Logan Sudeith became a full-time trader on prediction markets and in one month alone he managed to collect $250,000.

That doesn't happen from simply checking the odds of an event contract on the platform, he said. A clever trade requires tools.

"For the Super Bowl I bought an antenna, so that I could watch the commercials," he said, noting online streaming services could face lags. Sudeith was able to quickly trade on what companies would show ads during the largest televised U.S. sporting event, or what would be said during those commercials. "I wanted to have the lowest latency access to those."

Between Polymarket and Kalshi alone, there can be more than 100,000 active markets. That's too much for traders like Sudeith to juggle on their own. And that's why they don't.

CNBC spoke to several active traders on prediction market exchanges about how they gain an edge. From using AI bots to purchasing an antenna, traders rely on tools and peculiar methods to compete against others, and it's enough motivation for some to trade on the platforms full-time.

And while hedge funds and large institutional trading desks are known for using complicated tools that help them win in the market, these traders are often just one person doing the work from their homes.

Not every trader has the capacity to make custom workflows. That's why some platforms are offering more advanced technology to speculators, so that they don't have to build it all on their own.

But whether those new, accessible products can deliver the same results to what individuals have made for themselves is unclear.

One common theme among traders is reading the news. Kenneth Deneau, 32, calls it a "minimum requirement" to know what's happening in the world but admits that it can get overwhelming.

He turned to AI to scan relevant information, including the newsletters he's subscribed to and Discord servers, to find insight for potential trades.

"I think that has been probably one of the most transformative aspects of allowing me to do this now, being able to build out those tools," he said about Anthropic-owned language model Claude.

The surge in trading volume on Kalshi and Polymarket last fall drove Deneau to become a full-time prediction market trader. He left behind nearly a decade of work in institutional investing but carried over one key skill to his next gig: deep research under a time crunch.

Earlier this year, when an event contract asked the date for when President Donald Trump would fire former Attorney General Pam Bondi, Deneau relied on Pacer, a database providing court records, to figure it out before it became viral.

"If you found those filings, which I did, you could use that as a baseline to help you determine when [Bondi] actually left the office," Deneau said. "As far as I know, I was probably one of the first ones to take advantage of that."

Prediction market platforms have an Application Programming Interface, or API, that makes their live and closed markets accessible. It's a playground full of analysis for Atlanta-based data engineer Steve Farmer.

From his wife's "big closet", Farmer spent countless hours building an AI bot that would trade on Kalshi all day.

"As a trader, I wouldn't do very well myself because you know, impulses and greed and all that will just drive me nuts," he said. "A bot doesn't have all that."

His bot has about a 70% win rate in trading on economic-related event contracts on Kalshi, though he admitted it's likely not a long-term investment strategy, noting it's not replacing his retirement fund.

What it is, however, is "enough to pay for my AI bills," he said.

Michael Boss placed his first trades on Kalshi during the 2024 presidential election, and decided he wanted to start speculating more often on the platform in summer 2025. But he didn't start trading full-time until February this year, waiting until he had the necessary software.

The software Boss uses is placing many trades all the time across various markets. He wouldn't reveal exactly what he uses to train his software, showcasing just how much he wants to protect any edge he has over other traders.

"On something like Kalshi, a lot of different things need to go well," he said. "There's a ton of markets on Kalshi, so it's kind of a big problem to tackle in that way."

Prediction market exchanges know their most active traders have elaborate software and tools. Some platforms are looking to make trading easier for highly-engaged speculators.

Kalshi, for example, recentlylauncheda "Pro" trading terminal, which it says makes it easier to place trades faster and view data about individual markets.

Deekaraul "Deek" Harinath, a Kalshi speculator who has placed more than 5,700 trades on the platform, was part of a select group that tested the terminal before its official launch this month. He told CNBC he often trades on the 15-minute cryptocurrency contracts, which ask if Bitcoin prices will go up or down in a quarter hour.

"Everything is faster on the Pro, and that's a big deal for me," he said. Harinath said having the ability to only click once to submit a trade, a feature of Kalshi Pro, is also an upgrade.

Still, while Harinath plans to use Kalshi Pro to place manual trades, he also intends to develop a bot for automation purposes and place trades on various short-term contracts that he's too busy to participate in manually.

Beyond the two major exchanges, startups are also trying to convince traders their tools will give them that missing edge.

Jay Malavia is a co-founder and CEO at Kairos, an Andreessen Horowitz-backed prediction market trading terminal that allows speculators to trade across various exchanges, including Kalshi and Polymarket.

Malavia said the goal at Kairos is to offer strong technology to those who can't or don't know how to build it themselves.

"There's these big trading firms that are going to build the best tech in the world, and we are going to give you the closest technology to go and compete and win in these markets," he said.

Kairos allows traders to see different contracts and price moves across exchanges, as well as deliver real-time data and headlines across various events.

And while Kairos is geared to "democratizing" technology for prediction market traders who don't have their own, Malavia also said it can be a solution for highly active traders too. That's because Kairos takes on the job of maintaining the software rather than an individual having to do it.

So long as people are manually placing trades, Boss thinks a speculator will be behind those who have tools to do the work for them.

"Anything discretionary can be systematized," Boss said. "No person is going to be as competitive as good software."

Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

title: 费萨尔·伊斯兰：国际足联世界杯计划从未实现的四个原因
content: Image source,ReutersByFaisal IslamEconomics editorPublished2 hours agoDocuments that set out Fifa's plan to part-privatise the World Cup and seen by the BBC show why the deal may have fallen apart.The sales pitch was circulated to Fifa members this week, setting out the case for Gianni Infantino's controversial plan featuring pictures of the Spain team lifting the trophy and Argentina's fans.The 25-page deck of slides painted a picture of American football-level revenue expectations, which pointed to a potential continuation and extension of the controversial 2026 US-influenced World Cup model.It suggested there was the potential for $1,000+ tickets, dynamic pricing, and pressure to put broadcasting of the world's biggest sports tournament behind a paywall.The documents make it clear that the plan and Fifa's arguments never really stacked up. Here are four reasons why.1. The claim that football is 'under-monetised'In the slides, Fifa's central argument was that football does not raise enough cash in relation to its fan base, that "Fifa has been under-monetised versus other leagues" and so "global football development gets squeezed".It did this with reference to a comparative chart showing annual revenue as well as revenue per fan for Fifa, the Uefa Champions League, Premier League, US baseball and NFL American football.On the face of it, Fifa is the poorer cousin at just $1 per global fan, compared to NFL's $52.80. But this measure is rather suspect.The World Cup is not an annual competition - it happens once every four years. If instead this was done on revenue per World Cup 2026 match, Fifa makes multiples of the Premier League, perhaps more than three times as much.As important, football is decentralised globally, so more of the revenues go to individual leagues, such as the Premier League or Champions League. Fifa was effectively arguing it wanted to keep more of that overall football pie.Football's fans are also spread across the globe, in rich and poor countries alike. NFL has a much smaller base concentrated in the US and is pretty much the whole of American Football.Finally, about half of NFL's revenues are paid out as wages. Fifa does not pay Erling Haaland or Lionel Messi or Vozinha. Profits would have yielded a rather different result than the chartâs focus on revenues.2. Extraordinary ticket pricesAccording to the document, the new partly privatised entity, called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), would have become the "organiser and operator of competitions" - i.e. the World Cup - and would be responsible for ticketing, broadcast, licensing and sponsorship.That would have been a clear transfer of the organising power from a non-profit answerable to all of world football to a privately backed company, albeit one with majority of Fifa board members.The slides said that the FFE structure would "expand and optimise media rights monetisation" and "maximise the value of Fifa IP [Intellectual Property], which has been undermonetised, historically". This would have been a transfer of responsibility and accountability from Fifa itself.As Fifa highlighted the revenue per fan of the NFL in the document, it raised questions about a future of free-to-air World Cup games.This is protected by legislation in the UK and Europe, but digital rights will alter considerably in the coming years. It could also clearly have underpinned the continuation of the extraordinary ticket prices charged in 2026.Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?Published5 hours agoFifa executive joins Burnham in questioning InfantinoPublished17 hours agoFifa says 'nobody selling football' as plan continuesPublished1 day ago3. No stated fee for the 'annual licence payment'Why was Fifa trying to sell a $4.2bn (Â£3.1bn; â¬3.6bn) stake?Fifa had already said that it would give FFE a 20% stake in the organisation, which would raise an initial $4.2bn.The document made it clear that initial cash injection would fund the $20m "extraordinary distribution" to each of the 211 member associations.That explained the $4.2bn funding requirement. Essentially, the funding would have been used to provide a $20m one-off payment for infrastructure to every voting association that would have made the decision on Infantino's plan.It would have meant, for example, giving Montserrat a sum worth just under half its entire economy or $10,000 per person, and the same for, say, Bangladesh, a massive highly-populated growth market for global football development.Where would the extra money for investment in Fifa's future been, given the new investment would have been immediately distributed to voting members? How much would actually have been paid back to Fifa as an "annual license payment" referred to in a flow diagram in the charts, but not quantified? Would that have been fixed or proportionate to revenues?Did FFE have a mission to maximise revenues at all costs to provide returns for the investors?None of these crucial questions were answered by the document.4. The Kushner connectionThe private timetable shared in the document said that investors would be given access to the materials starting this month. Terms would have been confirmed by September, and bids and transfer of funds by the end of October. This showed how advanced the plans were, and the speed with which members were being asked to decide.The lead investors were publicly been named as Thrive Eternal, run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.Thrive was almost entirely concerned with AI investments, with OpenAI taking a stake in one of its arms.Thrive only began its sports investment arm in April, with an investment in the San Francisco Giants baseball team, which was the pioneer in sport-based dynamic pricing of tickets.Kushner said that the fund would focus on certain live sports as "these are assets with qualities that cannot be replicated by technology".This is an investment thesis that the value of certain forms of entertainment which can not be replaced by AI (unlike music or some films) will increase in the coming years.So in the end, we were left with an opaque structure designed to continue the 2026 experiment with high ticket prices, commercialisation whichwould put pressure on broadcast costs, and inevitably lead to more matches, and more frequent tournaments. A proposal that fell apart in a matter of days.Related topicsFifaMoneyMore on this storyCourting controversy and befriending Trump - the story of Fifa boss InfantinoPublished5 hours agoWhy the economics make this the craziest World Cup everPublished12 June

title: 随着美国人直接使用 GLP-1 处方，沃尔玛、好市多、亚马逊将成为减肥大赢家
content:
As more Americans use GLP-1 weight-loss drugs to shrink their waistlines, retail giants are betting on a bottom-line bump tied to a shift in the way the drugs are priced and purchased. Employers aredropping coverage for GLP-1 drugslike Wegovy and Zepbound in greater numbers, nudging more patients to direct-to-consumerprescription programs, and providing Walmart, Costco, CVS and Amazon the opportunity to gain a greater share of the market.

For the retail pharmacy chains, a GLP-1 prescription is evolving into more than a simple sale — it's creating a beachhead to developing customer relationships that can run for years and pull shoppers toward everything else on the shelf. If a customer is going to get their GLP-1s from Walmart, they might as well get all their other prescriptions and load up on deodorant, paper towels, and condiments.

"Retailers are betting that if they can become the front door for obesity care, they'll earn a relationship that extends far beyond a single GLP-1 prescription," said Eric Bormel, managing director specializing in digital healthcare at Solomon Partners' healthcare group.

The DTC GLP-1 programs are customer acquisition tools, Bormel said, and retailers are increasingly valuing the entire ecosystem around the medication more than the medication itself, which is experiencing downward price pressure.

"Everyone recognizes that obesity treatment is becoming a longitudinal consumer relationship," Bormel said, noting that retailers aren't simply fighting over the same customers, but bringing in new ones through the GLP-1 business. It's one of the business tailwinds that is in stark contrast toinitial concernsthat GLP-1s were a headwind for retailers as consumers cut back on impulse buys and overall grocery spending.

New clothing needsis one way that retailers stand to benefit from GLP-1 usage. But the need for prescription refills fits into an even broader strategy for large retail pharmacy networks that have been betting the weight-loss drug boom, even at low margins, will pay off for their businesses.

"In a retail industry that spends billions chasing foot traffic, that is the most reliable recurring customer relationship on the market," said Jackie Swanson, managing partner at Gartner Consulting.

Walmart becoming the retail pickup point for LillyDirect matters because the patient who collects a prescription walks through the store to reach it. "Pharmacy lock-in is loyalty-program economics applied to medicine, and it works because the refill, unlike almost everything else in retail, is non-negotiable," Swanson said.

She notes LillyDirect's cash prices, which run $299 to $449 a month, with the better pricing tied to refilling within 45 days. "Which is a loyalty program dressed as a discount schedule," Swanson said.

Novo Nordisk's NovoCare has a $199 price for introductory months, which later steps up to $349, a "classic acquisition funnel," Swanson said.

Meanwhile, Costco's Sesame partnership prices Wegovy at around $349 and requires a membership. "So the prescription now helps sell the $65 card," Swanson said.

Swanson says that, for customers, the discount is real, and for chains, what is a deal for customers is a deal for them, too: a minimal acquisition cost for a long-term relationship.

"When a discount is tied to a network, the patient's choice of pharmacy happens at sign-up, not at the counter, and that's a meaningful change for any pharmacy that has historically won business through service and proximity. The economics of these programs favor scale," Swanson said. "The retailer that fills the prescription tends to sell the groceries too, and pharmacy is quietly becoming the membership battleground of American retail," Swanson added.

Walmart, the nation's fifth-largest prescription provider with nearly 4,600 pharmacies, has moved aggressively to capture this shift. In April, the retailer expanded its Better Care Services digital platform to bundle GLP-1 prescriptions with weight-management support like nutrition coaching, fitness apps, and AI-driven coaching tools, while positioning itself as a one-stop destination rather than just a pickup counter. According to the most recent published data from Drug Channels Institute, a pharmacy industry research firm, Walmart currently holds 4.8% of the pharmacy market, well behind CVS's 14.7% and Walgreens' 14.6%. The DTC GLP-1 gives Walmart a new tool to try to catch up.

Amazon, which has spent years attempting to increase its healthcare footprint, is targeting the opportunity as well. In April, the company launched a GLP-1 management program through Amazon One Medical, the primary care business it acquired in 2022, and Amazon Pharmacy, offering insured patients prices as low as $25 a month and providing same-day delivery in nearly 3,000 cities, expanding to 4,500 by year's end.

Capital from retailers is flowing into weight-management platforms, virtual obesity care, nutrition coaching, metabolic health solutions, and employer care management programs.

The focus on GLP-1s from the major retailers is not new. As far back as 2023, then-Walmart CEO Doug McMillon said the company expectedweight loss drugs to help drive sales. But that didn't necessarily translate into profitability. "Sales dollars are a lot bigger than the margin dollars," said Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen at that time. "The impact on profitability is pretty narrow," he said.

The big retailers have also struggled in the past to capture a broader slice of the healthcare pie. Walmartshuttered its Walmart Health clinicsand virtual care service entirely in 2024, closing all 51 locations across six states after concluding the primary-care business wasn't sustainable amid reimbursement pressures and rising costs — five years after it first opened the clinics.

Amazon'shistory of healthcare effortsincludes shutting down its Amazon Care telehealth service at the end of 2022, just weeks after unveiling its $3.9 billion deal for One Medical. Years earlier, it walked away from Haven, its joint health care venture with JPMorgan Chase and Berkshire Hathaway, which dissolved in 2021 without producing the cost savings the three companies had promised.

CVS has had to shutter many of its instore Minute Clinics and the company has had itsshare of other strugglesover the years with trying to make healthcare as profitable as paper towels or back-to-school supplies.

Swanson said the timing of these DTC efforts dovetails with employers leaving the space. A survey by Mercer last month showed 6% of large employers dropped GLP-1 coverage this year, with the drugs' share of claims swelling to 11.4% from the 6.9% figure it was at in 2023. Moreemployers have balked at payingfor them because so many people could be eligible for the treatments and many patients stop them after achieving a weight-loss goal. Health insurance company Cigna said earlier this month it would stop covering the medicines for its own employees.

More employers are pointing workers to the direct-to-consumer platforms.

"Every patient who loses coverage is choosing a new front door for care this year, and retailers are competing to be that door at the exact moment of the decision. Real affordability gets delivered; a customer relationship gets acquired; both statements are true simultaneously," Swanson said.

Seth Friedman, pharmacy & health plan services practice leader at Gallagher, says on the other side of the opportunity for the retail chains are the independent pharmacies and non-chain players, who stand to be the big losers in this shift. "Smaller pharmacies stand to lose volume for sure," Friedman said.

Dared Price, who owns nine pharmacies located in small Kansas towns like Winfield, population 11,000, said he is already feeling the impact as customers race to the big chains for their GLP-1s. "It is frustrating to me to not be able to provide the same access to our patients that they do to CVS or Costco," Price said. "It puts independent pharmacies at a big disadvantage."

Price said the shift creates a potentially dangerous situation for some patients. "If one of my customers wants to do a DTC program and has to go to CVS or Costco, those pharmacies don't have access to the rest of their portfolio," Price said. Price, for his part, has no way of knowing whether a customer is taking GLP-1 drugs if they are getting them from big pharmacies. "My system won't flag any drug interactions with GLP drugs and there are drug interactions that can be dangerous," he said, adding it's a serious issue given that there are known interactions with other drugs like insulin or oral contraceptives that could be problematic.

CVS, however, says its pharmacists are ready to treat the whole patient. "Access is only part of the equation with GLP-1 medications. Patients also need support to stay on therapy and see results," said Sid Tenneti, senior vice president and interim president, pharmacy and consumer wellness, in a statement shared by a CVS spokesperson.

"Participation in NovoCare is one way we are assisting patients, but we are also participating in Medicare Bridge and accept most third-party prescription discount cards," the CVS spokesperson added.

That program, a new Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services initiative launched July 1, offering eligible Medicare patients GLP-1s for weight loss at a flat $50 monthly copay, runs through a single central processor rather than through a patient's regular pharmacy of record, the kind of structural gap that worries some obesity-care specialists.

title: OpenAI 的 Hugging Face 黑客事件证实了数月来的人工智能网络警告：“潘多拉魔盒已打开”
content:
几个月来，网络安全领导者警告人工智能将重塑威胁格局，将长达数周和数天的网络攻击压缩到几分钟内。

直到上周，这些威胁仍然感觉像是遥远的风险。

Hugging Face 上的 OpenAIagent 黑客事件表明，这个时代不仅已经到来，而且带来了新的挑战：AI 代理将走极端来实现其目标，并以不可预测的方式完成任务。

“现实是潘多拉魔盒已经打开，”Zscaler 首席信息安全官 Sam Curry 说道。 “我们需要表现得好像人工智能只是未来生活的一个事实。这些事情最多只会减慢它的速度。他们不会阻止它。”

近四个月前 Anthropic 强大的 Mythos 模型的推出引起了人们的担忧，即黑客可能会利用这些模型来利用漏洞。主要科技公司组成联盟，开始测试这种先进的人工智能，以便做好准备。

当时，Palo Alto Networks 的产品和技术主管 Lee Klarich 警告说，人工智能驱动的漏洞很快就会成为新常态，企业有三到五个月的时间来超越他们的敌人。

对于网络行业来说，“抱脸”事件发生的时机再合适不过了。

在接下来的一周，数千名行业专家齐聚拉斯维加斯参加今年最重要的网络安全活动之一的黑帽大会。这也是自 Mythos 级模型广泛发布以及政府更加关注人工智能安全以来该行业举行的首次重大会议。

在 Hugging Face 会议之后，企业不仅要问如何防御对手，而且还要面对这样一个严酷的现实：旨在保护其网络的人工智能系统也可能出现在意想不到的地方。

“我们已经从科幻小说变成了现实，”博思艾伦国家网络总裁 Brad Medairy 表示。

上周，OpenAI 披露其部分人工智能模型突破了沙盒测试环境。这些代理为了在内部测试中寻找信息作弊，破坏了开源开发者平台 Hugging Face 并访问了其他四个帐户来促成攻击。

Hugging Face 将此事件标记为首次处理由代理系统从头到尾主导的攻击，这表明攻击能力在没有人为干预的情况下已经变得多么先进。

几天后，Anthropic 发现了三个实例，其中其 Claude 模型“未经授权访问了三个不同的真实系统”专家表示，这并不是第一次由人工智能代理主导的攻击，但由于规模和知名度，它们引起了极大的关注。今年 4 月，软件初创公司 PocketOS 的创始人 Jer Crane 表示，该公司在自己的系统中使用的 Cursor AI 代理在 9 秒内就清除了其生产数据库和备份。

代码删除代表了更极端的情况，但 SailPointtech 首席执行官 Chandra Gnanasambandam 表示，人工智能获取权限的实例实际上比人们意识到的更常见，而且每天都在发生。

“我与客户进行的对话的性质与我们的客户不同。一个月前，”他说。 “他们更加意识到这个问题。”

更令人担忧的是，“抱脸”事件是迄今为止最清晰的例证之一，它说明了一个严峻的现实：人工智能不像人脑那样运作，而是会研究和适应智胜系统并实现目标。

几个月前，企业还担心对手使用人工智能进行攻击。客户现在质疑如何在不造成自我伤害的情况下引入人工智能，他们将在 Black Hat 中寻找答案。

网络安全初创公司 Zafran Security 的首席执行官 Sanaz Yashar 表示：“对于人工智能来说，这是非常简单的事情。” “我有一个使命：解决这个问题，我会杀死我面前的一切，或者绕过它。”

title: 由于伊朗威胁要切断航线，阿曼附近的油轮遭到攻击
content:
据报道，阿曼附近的一艘油轮夜间遭到袭击，另一艘油轮称，伊朗警告华盛顿，美军封锁霍尔木兹海峡将导致主要航线关闭。

另外，科威特表示，其防空系统遭遇了伊朗的敌对无人机袭击。

最近的冲突发生在美国媒体报道美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在准备的情况下。由于通过谈判结束 2 月 28 日开始的战争的希望逐渐消退，能源价格攀升，最早将于本周末对伊朗进行新一轮打击。

英国海军支持的组织英国海事贸易运营中心 (UKMTO) 周六表示，它收到了一艘油轮被“不明弹丸击中，造成机舱损坏”的报告。

“这艘油轮不受指挥，地区海岸警卫队也没有指挥。 UKMTO 谈到阿曼东北 11 海里处的这起事件时表示，目前尚未接到通知。

UKMTO 表示，阿曼附近海域的另一艘油轮报告“在该船附近看到大规模飞溅和爆炸”。

美国和伊朗 6 月 17 日签署谅解备忘录后的临时停火实际上已经破裂。双方在关键问题上都没有让步，包括伊朗核计划和对霍尔木兹海峡航运的控制，战争爆发前，世界上约五分之一的石油供应是通过霍尔木兹海峡运输的。

上周，美国完成了针对伊朗的“猛烈”打击，击中了数十个伊斯兰革命卫队目标。作为报复，伊朗袭击了美国在科威特和巴林的军事基地。

埃及周四表示，一架无人机击中了其地中海达米埃塔港的两艘船只，引发火灾。没有人声称对这次袭击负责，这是自战争开始以来埃及领土上发生的第一次袭击，也是冲突正在扩大的另一个迹象。

《华尔街日报》周五援引未透露姓名的美国官员的话说，特朗普已命令军方对伊朗发动新的袭击，最早可能在本周末开始。但官员们告诉《华尔街日报》，如果外交方面取得进展，特朗普可能会取消计划中的袭击。

美联社援引特朗普周五在戴维营总统度假胜地举行的电视内阁会议上的话说，“我们将非常严厉地打击他们”。 “你知道，在某个时候，他们会说，‘我们再也受不了了。’”

Axios 援引一位不愿透露姓名的美国官员的话说，特朗普正在认真考虑在未来几天内攻击伊朗能源目标，但尚未下达这样做的最终命令。

一位伊朗官员警告称，美国的行动将导致伊朗加强对关键海上的控制。伊朗WANA通讯社援引伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书穆罕默德·巴格尔·佐尔加德尔的话称，“美国政权继续实施海上封锁和好战行为，不仅会更紧地封锁霍尔木兹海峡，还会封锁其他海峡和咽喉要道。”

“为此付出的代价将由全球经济、能源市场、据报道，佐尔加德尔说道。

美国于 7 月 13 日重新对伊朗船只实施海上封锁，阻止其船只进出其港口。

伊朗支持的胡塞武装最近在也门发动的袭击以及周五在埃及的无人机袭击引发了人们的担忧，即红海南端至关重要的曼德海峡可能成为伊朗的第二个咽喉要道。双方在霍尔木兹海峡争夺战中，伊朗成为目标。

周五，西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨逾 1%，收于每桶 84.67 美元。国际基准布伦特原油也上涨逾 1%，收于每桶 90.12 美元。由于希望中东冲突能够缓和，周一价格遭到抛售，本周价格下跌超过 5%。

title: 伊朗权力中心重叠使得结束战争变得更加复杂
content:
自2月28日伊朗战争爆发以来的五个月里，每一次战斗的停顿都凸显了结束战争的复杂性。

6月17日的谅解备忘录开启了为期60天的关于霍尔木兹海峡、制裁以及伊朗核和导弹计划的谈判期，但由于伊朗对航运的攻击导致局势升级，几周内就出现了问题。

美国连续13晚恢复罢工，直到7月24日暂停，周二才恢复战斗，周三和周四连夜罢工。伊朗军队周五表示，已对科威特和巴林的美国战略资产和军事基地发动了袭击。

每当谈判恢复时，伊朗不透明的权力结构（涵盖最高领袖、革命卫队、文职政府、指挥官和其他团体）不仅会影响所达成的协议，还会影响协议的执行。

任何停火都必须经过各级指挥和伊斯兰革命卫队（伊朗革命卫队）指挥官和与德黑兰结盟的团体可能会对这些术语有不同的解释。本周，与伊朗结盟的伊拉克民兵对沙特石油设施的袭击以及也门胡塞武装对管道基础设施的袭击表明，同情伊朗的团体可能会扩大冲突。

对商业航运的袭击可能成为对伊朗战时力量平衡的早期考验。

美国一直强调，希望看到霍尔木兹海峡在不收费的情况下重新开放。虽然德黑兰的文官政府正在寻求经济救济和放松制裁，但安全机构内部的人士可能会将海峡的持续压力视为重要的杠杆来源。

伊朗文官政府希望解冻冻结的资金，为因数十年制裁而陷入困境的超过 9000 万伊朗人提供经济救济。

伊朗革命卫队长期以来一直受到伊朗革命卫队的破坏，萨纳姆说，伊朗革命卫队是“战争和国家安全的主导力量”。查塔姆研究所中东北非项目主任瓦基尔告诉 CNBC。

他们运营“导弹、无人机、情报网络和区域武装伙伴关系，在激烈冲突期间，其指挥官可以行使相当大的自主权，”她补充道。

“文职政府仍然很重要，总统可以制定外交、经济政策和最高国家安全委员会的工作，但他不指挥武装部队，”瓦基尔继续说道。

马苏德总统佩泽什基安领导伊朗文职政府，但国家安全的最终权力掌握在最高领袖阿亚图拉·阿里·哈梅内伊手中，而伊斯兰革命卫队则行使重要的行动自主权。

虽然最高领袖对国家安全拥有最终决定权，但“他并不亲自指挥每一项战术行动，”瓦基尔说。

伊斯兰革命卫队已成为伊朗占主导地位的军事和安全机构，负责监督导弹部队、无人机、区域行动以及与伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队结盟的武装团体的关系。德黑兰。它直接向最高领袖而不是文职政府负责。

它与伊朗常规军队并存，但在政治上更强大，并监督外国行动和伊朗的代理人，如真主党。至关重要的是，这些代理人通过武器、培训和资金输出伊斯兰共和国的意识形态。伊斯兰革命卫队还通过巴斯基准军事部队监督伊朗的内部安全。

本周标志着美国和沙特阿拉伯袭击伊拉克境内伊朗支持的民兵组织后暂时停止敌对行动的结束。伊朗对驻约旦美军发动突然导弹袭击，据美国军方称，所有导弹均被拦截。

这次袭击突显出，即使外交官试图重启谈判，冲突也会迅速扩大。

本周早些时候，外交官们试图给和平谈判“一些空间”。伊朗外交部发言人埃斯梅尔·巴格哈伊 (Esmail Baghaei) 周一表示，伊朗目前“没有与美国进行谈判”乔·拜登总统前高级顾问、TWG Global 执行合伙人阿莫斯·霍赫斯坦 (Amos Hochstein) 告诉 CNBC：“伊朗无意回到战前的现状。”

“停火不是一个可以简单扭转的开关。伊朗希望在将自己锁定在新的现状之前将战场现实转化为政治利益，”中东研究所高级研究员亚历克斯·瓦坦卡 (Alex Vatanka) 告诉 CNBC。

title: 因会员抵制，国际足联取消世界杯抛售计划
content:
国际足联周五表示，在该项目遭到一些成员协会的强烈抵制后，它将不会继续向外部投资者出售其商业帝国的一部分。

国际足联的计划是通过出售一个新部门约 20% 的股份来筹集至多 42 亿美元，该新部门将运营包括世界杯在内的国际足联赛事，估值为 20 美元

该提案于周二首次宣布，遭到了欧洲足球管理机构欧足联的强烈反对，欧足联威胁要抵制并指责国际足联将这项运动的“灵魂”出卖。

“在仔细听取了所有意见后，很明显，该项目已经造成了某种性质的分裂，无论支持程度如何，都不再符合第一个提案中设定的目标的利益。国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺在一份声明中表示。

“我们的目的一直是，也将永远是-团结和改进。因此，这项提议不会继续进行。”

周五早些时候，因凡蒂诺的高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗立即辞职，称该计划“对足球来说是一个糟糕的交易”。

国际足联首席运营官凯文·拉莫尔表示，工作人员被因凡蒂诺“欺骗”，称该提案是“一个人的项目”。

与此同时，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆周五告诉记者，因凡蒂诺“不是领导该组织的最佳人选”。

title: 皮罗表示，“安装缺陷”造成倒影池损坏，并准备撤销对奥林匹亚运动员的诉讼
content:
U.S. Attorney for the District of ColumbiaJeanine Pirroon Fridaymoved to dismissan indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeistDavid Hearnwith vandalizing theReflecting Poolof the Lincoln Memorial, writing in a court filing that damage to the pool's sealant was the result of a "flawed installation."

Pirro, in a court filing in D.C. Superior Court, said her office received information and evidence after the charges were filed that "significantly undermine the evidentiary basis for the indictment."

Hearn had been charged with felony destruction of property in early July, with Pirro saying at a press conference that he "violently" ripped up part of the pool's liner with his bare hands.

Hearn's attorneys accused the Trump administration of making the 67-year-old ex-Olympian a "scapegoat" for theexpensiveand troubled renovation, which PresidentDonald Trumphad frequently boasted about.

After the pool appeared to continue leaking following its renovation, Trump repeatedly claimed, without providing evidence, that vandals had cut a gash hundreds of feet long along the bottom.

But Pirro said in Friday's court filing that a "botched installation" was to blame.

Prosecutors had presented a grand jury in D.C. with "evidence that damage to the Reflecting Pool was caused by vandals" after receiving initial reports to that effect from the Department of the Interior and the U.S. Park Police, Pirro wrote.

But after that grand jury returned its indictment against Hearn, the Interior Department provided "additional documents" showing that the damage occurring in June was the "result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings," Pirro said.

She also blamed "the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration in the weeks surrounding Independence Day 2026."

Asked for additional comment, the U.S. Attorney's Office for D.C. told CNBC, "The motion speaks for itself."

Hearn's attorneys told CNBC in a statement, "The Trump administration's case against Davey Hearn should have never been brought."

"Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong," read the statement from lawyers Norm Eisen, Mary Dohrmann and Steve Levin.

"The government's approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology," they said.

The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

Four days earlier, Hearn's attorneyswrote in a court filingthat the government's key grand-jury witness in the case "testified that the property was already damaged before Mr. Hearn allegedly touched it."

In that same filing, the defense lawyers asked for the disclosure of the information that the government provided to the grand jury before it made the decision to charge Hearn.

Pirro's decision to pack up her case may foreclose the possibility of that information being revealed.

Her filing repeatedly and pointedly lays blame on the Interior Department for providing her office with shoddy information.

"DOI provided less than fulsome information at the outset of this case," Pirro wrote at one point. "It was not until USAO-DC repeatedly reached out to DOI dozens and dozens of times that DOI slowly started trickling information to USAO-DC."

"Had DOI been forthcoming with the information clearly in its possession, the government would not have sought a grand jury indictment," she wrote. "DOI's failure to fully and accurately provide information to USAODC undermined the government's ability to abide by these responsibilities."

The Interior Department did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

Pirro's motion to dismiss also provides new detail about issues that plagued the Reflecting Pool renovation and caused delays "almost immediately."

She pointed to "a combination of very rainy and windy weather, repeated failures of testing on the sealing of the expansion joints, and delays in obtaining sealing product at the worksite."

"The rush to complete the project led to hasty and botched work that was not remediated before the project was finished and the fencing removed," Pirro wrote.

The Trump administration had awarded the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings LLC, ano-bid contractto work on the Reflecting Pool.

Trump, in one of numerous instances detailing the renovation project to the press,said in Aprilthat he chose a contractor that had worked on one of his swimming pools.

CNBC has requested comment from the contractor. A website associated with the company currently features a pop-up window with two Reflecting Pool-related updates, with the most recent one dated June 21.

"Atlantic Industrial Coatings in conjunction with the US Park Service has identified some areas in the Reflecting Pool that require repairs," the update reads. "These areas are a very small part of the massive 7 acre project, and do not indicate a failure of the liner."

title: Snapchat 与其他流行平台一起对抗“人工智能滥用”
content: 图片来源，路透社图片说明，Snapchat 正试图压制人工智能生成的视频。作者：Kali Hays 科技记者 2 小时前发布 Snapchat 已加入 YouTube、LinkedIn 和 Substack 等公司的行列，不断努力打击完全由人工智能 (AI) 工具创建的虚假文字、图像和视频。随着科技行业竞相创造更多更容易生成的内容，此类内容（通常称为“AI slop”）在网上激增。使用生成人工智能工具，可以创建从文章到逼真视频的任何内容。Snapchat 的母公司 Snap 周五表示，该平台将停止在其受欢迎的 Spotlight 提要中推荐“完全由人工智能生成的视频”，转而支持“真实的、人造内容”。过去两周，YouTube、LinkedIn 和 Substack 都公布了类似的策略。Snap 并没有试图禁止 Snapchat 上的所有人工智能生成内容。该平台提供自己的人工智能工具来更改内容，因此人工智能“增强或编辑”的内容仍将是其向用户推荐的一部分。不过，Snap 承认，完全由人工智能生成的内容通常是“低质量”、“重复”的，通常不是 Snapchat 用户想要看到的内容。最近对人工智能生成内容的接受情况的研究表明，人们倾向于同意这些描述。此外，人们在社交媒体源中看到的人工智能生成内容越假，然而，根据另一项调查，外部人士认为他们在网上看到的任何内容都是真实的。 针对“AI 溢出” 正如 Substack 联合创始人兼首席执行官克里斯·贝斯特 (Chris Best) 上周所说：“辨别互联网上的真实内容变得越来越困难。”外部宣布推出一种新工具，旨在让时事通讯平台上的读者检测人工智能生成的写作，贝斯特引用了其他研究，该研究发现多达 40%贝斯特说：“奖励虚假信息的平台将引发逐底竞争。”专注于工作的社交媒体平台LinkedIn本周在其平台上推出了一个按钮，允许任何用户报告是否有帖子或评论似乎是人工智能生成的。“人工智能垃圾是我们所有人的首要任务，”LinkedIn首席产品官哈里·斯里尼瓦桑(Hari Srinivasan)在该平台上写道。在过去的几个月里，他表示该平台已经“阻止了数十亿次”发布人工智能生成的评论的尝试。斯里尼瓦桑说：“我们现在每天都会捕获数十万条自动评论尝试。”与 Snap 一样，LinkedIn 也表示，它并不完全拒绝使用人工智能，使用人工智能工具“完善”其帖子的用户不应陷入对抗人工智能滥用的努力中。尽管如此，LinkedIn 正在删除一个自动提示，该提示会在用户撰写帖子时显示，旨在通过使用人工智能“增强”帖子。它将回归到一个简单的校对工具。谷歌旗下的视频平台 YouTube 也在本月更新了政策，围绕什么样的内容可以被创作者货币化。去年的研究发现，YouTube 上有数十个频道完全是人工智能生成的内容，其中许多频道拥有数百万订阅者，其中一些频道赚取了数百万美元的收入。为了阻止 YouTube 充斥该平台所谓的“不真实内容”，本月早些时候，该网站崩溃了将不允许通过其赚钱的视频分为三类：通用、重复或基于模板。使用生成式人工智能工具，这些风格的内容更容易制作，而且速度更快。YouTube 的信任和安全主管马特·哈尔普林 (Matt Halprin) 在接受采访时表示，更新后的规则表明，虽然人工智能工具可以帮助人们处理内容，但它们更常被用来制作虚假和低质量的视频。“同样的技术确实可以实现伟大的东西，”哈尔普林”说。“但它也使内容农业成为可能，而这正是我们不想拥有的东西。”相关主题SnapchatYouTubeGoogleLinkedIn人工智能虚假信息社交媒体更多关于这个故事的人工智能“slop”正在改变社交媒体 - 强烈的反对正在酝酿2月4日发布

title: 随着监管争论加剧，特朗普的人工智能行政命令接近关键期限
content:
当唐纳德·特朗普总统于 6 月初签署人工智能行政命令时，他给了联邦机构 60 天的时间来开发一个关键框架，作为其实施的一部分。

8 月 1 日的最后期限迅速临近，这在硅谷备受期待，最近几天，硅谷关于人工智能监管的争论一直在激烈进行。华盛顿特区，本周，所有人都试图影响即将做出的决定。

特朗普的行政命令缺乏细节，要求人工智能公司在公开发布之前自愿向政府提交其模型进行评估。总统责成财政部长斯科特·贝森特、国防部长皮特·赫格斯、白宫办公厅主任苏西·威尔斯、商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克和其他官员敲定具体细节。

当被问及对该框架的现状发表评论时，白宫将 CNBC 转至发言人库什·德赛的社交媒体帖子：“突发事件：特朗普政府将在我们为自己设定的最后期限内完成任务。”

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 没有立即回应置评请求。

Altmant 在周三告诉 CNBC，他已经看到了该框架的草案，并且就提议的更改而言，他没有“任何具体想法”。据报道，他在访问期间会见了 Wiles，预计还会见 Bessent 和 Lutnick。

截止日期是在美国人工智能发展的紧张时刻到来的，因为科技行业最有权势的领导者正在权衡人工智能应该如何监管，以及领先的模型开发商 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 是否应该能够对未来发挥巨大的影响力。

最近几周，市场经历了戏剧性的变化。所谓的开放权重模型（主要来自中国）正在展示它们的能力提升速度有多快。这些模型为 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的前沿模型提供了经济高效的替代方案，并允许用户下载技术、修改技术并在自己选择的基础设施上运行。

这些发展引发了科技行业内关于特朗普政府是否应该采取行动限制或彻底禁止中国开放权重模型的激烈争论。全球领先的科技高管以几乎前所未有的方式一致反对任何潜在的禁令。

英伟达的黄仁勋周一发布了一封信，敦促政策制定者避免对开放权重模型进行“过早限制”，从而加剧了讨论。黄以此为契机，在 X（以前的 Twitter）上首次发布帖子。

通过他的火箭公司 SpaceX 控制 X 的埃隆·马斯克回应说，“我全力支持。詹森是对的。”

微软、Meta、Palantir 和其他数十家公司签署了这封信。 OpenAI 后来加入，但 Anthropic 没有加入，而是选择在单独的博客文章中概述其立场。

特朗普政府尚未正式公开其在此事上的立场，尽管在政府中仍有影响力的前人工智能沙皇戴维·萨克斯 (David Sacks) 一直是任何形式禁令最强烈的反对者之一。

根据特朗普的行政命令，人工智能框架将涉及一个分类基准测试流程，该流程将评估模型的网络能力并确定它们是否符合模型的网络能力。应被视为“覆盖边境模型”。它还将鼓励公司与政府合作，确定能够访问这些模型的“值得信赖的合作伙伴”。

最终框架对于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 来说都是可喜的消息，自特朗普首次签署该命令以来，他们一直在经历一个模糊的模型部署流程。

行政命令发布后不久，Anthropic 不得不禁止访问其 Fable 5 和 Mythos 5 模型，以遵守美国政府发布的出口管制指令。商务部。两周后，OpenAI 表示，应美国政府的要求，它同意将其 GPT-5.6 模型系列的推出仅限于一组“值得信赖的合作伙伴”。两家公司最终都能够更广泛地推广他们的模式。

“政府和私营部门以我们从未见过的方式合作，这种美国优先的基础是前所未有的，”怀尔斯在六月下旬的一篇罕见的帖子中写道。 “我们共同的首要任务仍然是：尽可能快速、安全地部署最好的技术。”

观看：OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 本周将与白宫办公厅主任 Susie Wiles 会面

title: 随着亚马逊股价飙升，标准普尔 500 指数周五收高；道指连续第四个月上涨：实时更新
content:
The major averages were markedly higher Friday, the last trading session in July, as investors looked past rising bond yields andAmazonshares jumped.

TheNasdaq Compositerose 1% to end at 25,373.85, while theS&P 500added 0.7% to close at 7,489.72. TheDow Jones Industrial Averagegained 276.97 points, or 0.53%, to 52,485.03.

The30-year Treasury bond yieldspiked to its highest levels since 2007 this week. It was last up about 4 basis points on the day at 5.25%. The benchmark10-year Treasurynote yield topped 4.7% on the day, its highest level since January 2025.

The moves come as investors lost faith in Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's commitment to curb inflation, leading yields to jump. While Warsh indicated he is committed to the inflation fight, he did say this week, "We've got no magic wand."

"As [the yield for 10-year Treasury bonds] moves toward five percent, five percent is perhaps a level that will cause angst for sentiment and pressure valuations," Terry Sandven, chief equity strategist at US Bancorp Asset Management, told CNBC.

The strategist underscored that this "is a roller coaster market filled with angst and opportunity."

"On one hand, there's much to like about the market environment. Inflation is relatively steady, interest rates are range bound, and earnings are robust," Sandven said. "Conversely, you've got Middle East conflict, the Middle East conflict that continues, and that's pushing oil prices higher, which of course is inflationary."

West Texas Intermediate crude futuresrose about 1.3% to settle at $84.67 a barrel, while internationalBrent futuresadvanced 1.2% to $90.12 a barrel.

Hyperscaler and other artificial intelligence-related companies' earnings also colored investor sentiment.

Amazon surged 15% afterreporting better-than-expectedsecond-quarter revenue. The results, which were aided by the strength of its cloud-computing business, reinforced investor confidence in artificial intelligence spending.

Apple, in contrast, was more than 7% lower. The firm's fiscalthird-quarter revenue topped expectations, helped by a 22% jump in iPhone sales, though a shortfall in service revenue pushed its stock lower.

The moves followed a powerful rally during Thursday's session led byMicrosoft— which jumped 16% after the software giant posted stronger-than-expected Azure cloud growth. The recovery came after a bruising session on Wednesday, when theDow plunged more than 1,100 points, its worst one-day decline since April 2025.

Despite the week's sharp swings, the major averages remained on track to finish higher. The Dow was up about 1% for the week, along with the S&P 500. The Nasdaq Composite climbed about 1.6%.

However, the S&P 500 dropped 0.1%, and the Nasdaq fell 3.2%. The Dow was up 0.3% in July, notching its fourth consecutive positive month.

The three major indexes closed higher on Friday.

TheDow Jones Industrial Averageadvanced 0.53%, or about 276.97 points, to finish at 52,485.03. TheS&P 500settled up 0.7% to 7,489.72, while theNasdaq Compositesurged 1% to end the session at 25,373.85.

Semiconductors are on pace for their worst month since 2008, in spite of Friday's gains. TheVanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)was last lower by 16.9% month to date.

The slump continues asSpaceXlost over 36% of its value in the last month.

This comes after the aerospace manufacturer and stockalso fell from its June highof $225.64 to $113.50 last Monday, leaving the company's total market value to shrink more than $1.2 trillion.

Aside from a few days after SpaceX's debut public offering, its stock has seen a decline in value in the last month. Shares dropped over 3.5% as of Friday afternoon.

"Magnificent Seven" darling Microsoft is tracking for its best month in almost 19 years.

Following the company's post-earnings surge on Thursday, and additional gains on Friday, the stock is now on track to rise more than 20% in July. That's the biggest rise in a single month since October 2007 for shares of Microsoft.

As of Wednesday, Microsoft was only up just over 1.5% on the month, but the stock surged 15% on Thursday following the company'sfiscal fourth-quarter earnings report. Investors came away from that reportmore confident in Microsoft's artificial intelligence strategy.

Microsoft added to those gains on Friday, up another 2.5%.

TheNasdaq-100fell approximately 7% in July, recording its steepest monthly decline since March 2025, when it lost 7.69%.

The index previously declined 4.89% in March 2026 and 2.32% in February but both those losses were followed by sharp rebounds of 15.64% in April and 10.49% in May this year. The momentum, however faded with a 0.19% decline in June, before falling to 6.95% in July.

Uncertaintysurrounding the war in Iran, volatile oil prices, a hawkish Federal Reserve, anda sharp semiconductor sell-offweighed on the tech-heavy index. Investors have been concerned about the lofty tech valuations and whether surging AI spending will generate adequate returns.

The U.S. dollar is close to the session low against the Japanese yen at 158.15.

Thursday's low of 157.96 was the lowest level since May 14. Week-to-date the dollar is down 3.3% versus the yen, on pace for the biggest weekly slide since July, 2024.

Japanese monetary authorities likely intervened in currency markets this week to prop up the yen as traders braced Friday for another potential mediation.

"Japan's Ministry of Finance seemingly intervened in foreign exchange markets in defense of the yen," UBS economist Paul Donovan wrote in a Friday analysis. "This may have been more about the pace of weakness than any specific level."

Democratic senators on Friday demanded information on more than a dozen critical mineral deals with the federal government that potentially benefit the families of PresidentDonald Trumpor Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

The federal government is working on deals with at least 14 companies that have financial ties to the Trump or Lutnick families, the senators said, pointing to aNew York Timesinvestigation in June. The Trump administration has provided or is considering providing more than $8.9 billion in funding to the companies, according to the Times.

The senators asked the Departments of Commerce, Defense, Energy, Interior and the Export-Import Bank of the United States to preserve all records and communications related to those deals.

ExxonMobilandChevronon Friday reported second-quarter profits that surged on rising oil prices due to the Iran war.

Chevron's net income soared to $12 billion, a nearly 400% increase compared to $2.5 billion in the same period last year. Adjusted earnings came in at $6.06 per share, 50 cents higher than Wall Street's estimates.

"We're kind of firing on all cylinders, which is good, because the world needs it," CEO Mike Wirth told CNBC's Becky Quick.

Chevron shares rose about 1%, while Exxon shares were down more than 2%.

Shares ofNovo Nordiskfell as much as 10% on Friday after the drugmaker said a late-stage heart drug trial failed to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events, or MACE, compared to a placebo.

While the experimental medicine, ziltivekimab, did show some biological effect, it didn't translate into a statistically meaningful reduction in MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke, for patients with certain diseases,Novo said in a statementon Friday.

The missed endpoint is the latest blow to the Danish drugmaker, which is racing to restore investor confidence in its pipeline and ability to execute, especially in the challenging U.S. market.

Shares ofReplimunesurged 133% after a Food and Drug Administration advisory committeebacked the resultsof the clinical-stage biotechnology company's skin care trial.

The panelvoted 10-3on Thursday in favor of Replimune's drug, RP1, which the FDA has alreadydeclined to approve twice. The company is trying to get accelerated approval with RP1 to use withBristol-Myers Squibb's Opdivo for patients with advanced melanoma.

The FDA is expected to decide on the drug's approval by Aug. 2.

An ETF made up of all women-led companies hit an intraday all-time high of 39.44 on Friday. TheHypatia Women CEO ETF, which launched in June 2023, holds names such asnVent,Arista Networks,Exponent,Seaport TherapeuticsandFranklin Resources— all of which are up 3% or more on Friday.

The ETF has gained nearly 20% so far this year, more than double than theS&P 500's year-to-date performance.

Consumer sentiment perked up a bit in July as inflation fears abated, the University of Michigan reported Friday.

TheSurvey of Consumersposted a 55.2 reading for the end of the month, rising 11.5% from a month ago and better than the Dow Jones consensus for 54.0. However, it was still 10.5% below the same period in 2025. Current conditions and expectations indexes produced similar monthly gains.

On inflation, the one-year view dipped to 4.2%, down 0.4 percentage point from May and the lowest since March. The five-year outlook was unchanged at 3.3%.

"Despite recent gains, sentiment is 11% below a year ago, reflecting a generally somber view of the economy amid five years of elevated inflation and persistent high prices," said survey director Joanne Hsu. "Consumers remain focused on pocketbook issues like purchasing power, while political or military developments remain more in the background."

title: 特朗普称美国“不同意”授予乌克兰爱国者导弹许可证
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五表示，美国“尚未同意”授予乌克兰生产爱国者导弹系统的许可证，这显然背离了基辅对俄战争的首要任务之一。

特朗普在戴维营举行的内阁会议上表示，先进的军事技术“很难放弃”，并补充说，接受这些技术的国家“有一天可能会攻击你。”

“必须非常小心，”特朗普说。他说，美国和乌克兰仍在“讨论此事”。

特朗普对东欧战争的最新评论是在他在白宫与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基交谈三天后发表的。泽伦斯基表示，两国领导人就爱国者许可证问题进行了“良好的会晤”。

特朗普的明显转变也是在人们越来越担心美国正在消耗其顶级武器库存的背景下发生的，其中包括爱国者队继续在伊朗发动战争，防空系统是阻止伊朗导弹的关键。

不到三周前，特朗普直接告诉泽伦斯基，美国会满足他的愿望。特朗普在北约峰会上表示，“我们将向你们颁发制造爱国者导弹的许可证”，不过他补充说，“我们还没有通知该公司这件事”，可能指的是国防承包商洛克希德马丁诺RTX，这两家公司都生产导弹系统。

但周四，特朗普告诉英国《金融时报》，他“不确定”是否会继续让基辅建造“非凡的导弹”

乌克兰美国大使馆没有立即回应 CNBC 对特朗普最新言论发表评论的请求。

泽连斯基表示，爱国者系统对于乌克兰拦截来自俄罗斯的弹道导弹的能力至关重要。但即使乌克兰获得开始制造爱国者的许可，可能还需要数年时间才能在那里实际生产任何昂贵、高度复杂的武器。

泽伦斯基周五在与副总统万斯通话后表示，这个问题仍然是基辅的首要任务。

泽伦斯基在 X 帖子中写道：“我们同意我们的团队将保持联系并完成今天讨论的所有事情。” “我感谢美国对乌克兰和我们人民的支持。”泽伦斯基后来表示，他会见了洛克希德公司的团队，讨论了“我们与爱国者和其他系统相关的联合能力。”

他说：“我们的团队已经在制定具体的解决方案，以尽快转向联合生产，并提高我们保护生命的能力。”

洛克希德公司和 RTX 没有立即回应 CNBC 的要求。评论。

title: 金融科技经纪商 Clear Street 为投资者提供 IPO 前投资 1,880 亿美元人工智能巨头 Databricks 的机会
content:
Clear Street 是一家大宗经纪初创公司，最近搁置了自己的 IPO 计划，现在的目标是让投资者在硅谷一些最热门的私营公司上市之前能够接触到这些公司。

该公司即将宣布一个新平台，旨在让合格的投资者购买后期私营公司的权益，首先是人工智能软件巨头 Databricks，本月估值为 1880 亿美元，CNBC 是第一个

“我们的目标是消除摩擦，让更多人有能力投资更多产品，”Clear Street 首席执行官兼联合创始人尤里·科恩 (Uri Cohen) 在接受采访时表示。 “很多财富创造都发生在私募市场，越来越多的散户投资者和小投资者希望参与其中。”

越来越多的初创公司保持私有状态的时间更长，这意味着它们的大部分价值创造是在首次公开募股之前发生的。这刺激了富有的投资者在 Databricks、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等公司在公开市场首次亮相之前寻求投资的需求不断增长。

上周，CNBC 报道称，高盛创建了一个新平台，为越来越希望直接持有快速增长的私营公司的富裕客户和家族办公室扩大其产品范围。

Clear Street 通过在内部处理资产服务和风险管理，可以针对 IPO 前持有的资产提供保证金贷款，科恩表示，到年底，这家金融科技公司的平台上将有多达 30 家初创公司，其中大部分是估值在 50 亿至 200 亿美元之间的科技公司，距离首次公开募股大约需要六个月到两年的时间。

为了支持这一努力，Clear Street 还启动了由分析师 Owen Lau 领导的专门的私人公司股权研究，科恩称此举是为了将公开市场式的透明度带入传统领域。不透明的私募市场。

这次扩张正值 Clear Street 本身的关键时刻。

该公司今年早些时候在一轮私募融资中估值近 120 亿美元，但由于市场波动较大，经纪商和金融科技倍数倍受打击，该公司于 2 月份暂停了自己的 IPO 计划。

尽管暂停上市，但该公司现金流为正，并通过 4 亿美元的投资级债券增强了流动性科恩说：“我们处于有利地位，因此该决定被搁置，以便找到更好的时机。” “我们肯定会考虑在 27 年上市，具体取决于市场状况。”

title: 分析：市场听到了鸽派的凯文·沃什 (Kevin Warsh) 的言论。美联储主席自己的话暗示加息
content:
The overwhelming response toFederal ReserveChairmanKevin Warsh'scomments on Wednesday was that he would go easy oninflation. Investors who drove up bond yields in response should be careful.

Looking closely at what he said, Warsh may not be as dovish as widely believed. If inflation continues to come in above target, then Warsh — judging by his own words — may feel compelled to act soon to restrain the economy. Investors who act on what they thought they heard risk being blindsided if a rate increase is around the corner.

Crucially, Warsh opted not to celebrate a soft inflation print that had come in prior to the meeting. Had he wanted to present a dovish message, he could have seized on that data. Instead, he wrote it off.

Warsh's muddled performance Wednesday at his second press conference scrambled many investors' view of theFederal Reserve. Some saw a man who had been long perceived as an inflation hawk appear to talk down worries about inflation. He answered reporters' questions with vague statements and left many confused.

Some concluded Warsh is in thrall to PresidentDonald Trump, who continues to ask the Fed for lower interest rates, despite the central bank's statutory independence and pledges from both the president and Warsh that independence remains.

A chorus of market analysts said Warsh performance called hiscredibility into question.Long-term treasury yieldsrose, while the dollar fell and gold rose.

But if the market is misreading the Fed chairman as a dove, it could be in for further violent moves when traders are forced to unwind their positions. It helps to look at the prepared statement Warsh read out at the beginning of the press conference that reflected the message he went into the room intending to send — rather than what emerged from the back-and-forth with reporters.

Ahead of the meeting, theconsumer price indexshowed a rare decline, with prices falling by 0.4% in June from the month before.

Warsh was muted on that point."We understand that the five-plus years of inflation above target cannot be cured in nine weeks — or by a single month of modest price decreases," he said Wednesday, speaking for the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets the Fed's benchmark interest rate.

The words of Fed chairs are among the most carefully parsed remarks in the world. Warsh's performance Wednesday shows he hasn't yet figured out how to rhetorically separate the short-term and long-term challenges. Nor did his exchanges with reporters bolster his prepared remarks. Instead, he undermined himself and his carefully crafted message.

Investors were hoping to hear a chairman who would strike a hasty blow against fast-rising prices and speak up to a president who continues to bear down on the Fed. Investors didn't get that on Wednesday. Instead they heard about his plans to tinker with inflation measurements, and panicked.

But that isn't to say Warsh didn't try or intend to deliver the message that he was willing to raise rates.

"Where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act," Warsh said in his prepared remarks.

It is easy to dismiss that kind of language as empty hand-waving. But in 2012, then-Chairman Ben Bernanke — one of Warsh's mentors —pledgedto "provide additional policy accommodation as needed," and then proceeded to launch a new round of massive asset purchases. In May 2022, Jerome Powelltold reportersthat "we will not hesitate" to raise interest rates if necessary. In June, he hiked rates by three-quarters of a point.

Warsh has often spoken of the tremendouspromise of AIto produce growth without inflation. But in his prepared remarks, Warsh was more circumspect. He said it wasn't clear when the economy's productive capacity would be able to jump in response to all the spending that's happening now. As he put it, "the precise timing and magnitude of effects on the supply side remain hard to predict."

Warsh also spoke more clearly in his opening remarks about a point some analysts seized on in his later responses to reporters. The Fed's formal commitment on prices is to achieve 2% annual inflation over the long run as measured by thepersonal consumption expenditures index.

Asked about PCE, Warsh gave some observers the impression that he might change the 2% target. We are sticking with PCE for now, Warsh said. But, "who knows, come after next January, what we might say about strategy."

But Warsh showed no ambiguity in his prepared remarks. "There is no soft inflation target, there is no soft implicit target — not on this Committee's watch. There is only a target, and it is 2 percent."

So what is the Fed chairman prepared to do about it? There, too, his opening remarks dropped hints. The FOMC didn't just discuss interest rates, Warsh said. "We discussed monetary policy tools and strategies for achieving stable prices." The committee, Warsh explained, asked, "how much accommodation are we getting from the balance sheet?"

In other words, Warsh has already begun the task of moving the FOMC toward his long-stated goal of shrinking the Fed's balance sheet. As he hassaid elsewhere, that would effectively tighten financial conditions, similar to the effects of raising interest rates.

Theissue of the balance sheetspeaks to Warsh's challenge: He doesn't have the power to quickly push through the changes he wants. Warsh came into the Fed with an agenda for "regime change," as he described it. But the mechanism to achieve that change is a set of slow-moving task forces that he believes will sooner or later nudge the Fed into his preferred reforms. He wants to reduce the balance sheet, find alternate ways to measure inflation and get ready for an economy reshaped by AI.

But the task forces won't report back before the end of the year at the earliest. The committee clearly isn't ready to take action on the balance sheet. Warsh's explicit discussion of the Fed's "tools" is a strong indication he will take the earliest possible opportunity to use the balance sheet to tighten monetary policy, in addition to anything he might do on interest rates.

Meanwhile Warsh has to deal with an economy battered by tariffs and high energy prices that he can't influence directly, and by an AI boom whose potential fruits are still over the horizon.

Warsh has spent decades studying the leaders of the Fed and their failures. Credibility is paramount to him. His words suggest he may be further down the path to a rate hike than investors interpreted following Wednesday's meeting — and might just be waiting for the two inflation reports that come before the FOMC gathers next in September.

Given the beating he took in the aftermath of this meeting, it likely won't take him much to pull the trigger on a rate increase at the next one.

title: 被黑公司老板表示，人工智能公司必须对流氓机器人负责
content: 图片来源，盖蒂作者：Joe Tidy 网络通讯员，BBC World Service 2小时前发布最近被失控的人工智能 (AI) 攻击的一家公司的老板表示，机器人制造商必须对其创造的网络攻击负责。Clement Delangue 的公司 Hugging Face 被一个流氓 OpenAI 机器人入侵，该机器人本月早些时候突破了测试环境并自主攻击了他的公司。Hugging Face 不得不在这起史无前例的事件发生后，他将重建大约三分之一的 IT 网络。他告诉 CNN，他的公司（一家小型初创公司）不会对 OpenAI 采取法律行动，但他补充说，此类黑客行为是非法的，而且应该继续如此。他说：“每个人都必须记住，网络攻击是一种犯罪，而且是非法的。”德兰格表示，他希望法律框架能够确保犯下导致黑客错误的公司“承担责任”。他补充说，他不希望对其他公司进行网络攻击在他发表此番言论之前，聊天机器人 Claude 的制造商 Anthrophic 也承认，近几个月来，其机器人攻击了三家类似情况的公司。Anthropic 周五透露，在对最近的 OpenAI 事件进行审查后，才意识到自己的机器人已经逃脱了遏制系统，并入侵了这些组织。在这两种情况下，这两家人工智能巨头都不知道他们的模型在攻击发生很久之后才在互联网上漫游攻击公司。他们测试了他们的黑客技能，并通过突破看似安全的“沙箱”来在互联网上搜索完成研究人员设定的任务的方法来进行攻击。这些史无前例的事件在网络安全和法律界引发了激烈的争论，争论的焦点是谁（如果有的话）应该为失控的人工智能代理的攻击负责。 Pillar Security.Sarig 担心责任已经变得“模棱两可”。“今天，该行业正在给予宽限，但第一次由自主代理造成涉及真实数据、真实原告和真实财务损失的泄露，责任将不再是学术辩论，”他说。“那时，法律框架而不仅仅是技术保障措施将受到压力测试。”由于担心日益强大的自主系统带来的风险，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三表示，在最近发生的网络安全事件后，华盛顿正在考虑采取措施控制人工智能工具。此前，Hugging Face 的联合创始人托马斯·沃尔夫 (Thomas Wolf) 告诉 BBC，这一事件对整个行业来说是“一记警钟”。在他的机器人失控后，OpenAI 老板萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 表示，“我们可能不得不加快人工智能开发的速度”，但并未承诺放慢公司的发展速度。 OpenAI 已被要求发表评论，但一位发言人此前曾表示：“我们认识到关于该事件有很多问题和推测性细节在流传”。他们补充道：“我们计划在未来几周内发布一份有关我们所学知识的技术报告。”学习发布19小时前

title: 由于沃什领导的美联储面临对通胀采取行动的压力，这些指标显示通胀处于多年来的最低水平
content:
6 月份的定价数据表明，除了成本持续增长的某些特定项目之外，通胀正在回归美联储的通胀目标。

所谓的修剪均值指标（排除了价格上涨和下跌中的异常值）显示通胀处于本世纪初以来的最低水平。

事实上，达拉斯联储的指标将 6 月份的一个月年化利率仅为 1.4%，下降了 1.4%。较 5 月份飙升 1.3 个百分点，创 2020 年 11 月以来的最低水平。

此外，美联储政策制定者更密切关注的 12 个月利率降至 2.2%，较一个月前下降 0.2 个百分点，创 2021 年 7 月以来的最低水平。

虽然美联储官员很快强调，他们并不关注任何一个月的数据点，但截尾均值的趋势可能会影响引起一些关注，特别是考虑到主席凯文·沃什打算重新审视央行如何看待通胀及其使用的数据点。

花旗集团经济学家安德鲁·霍伦霍斯特在一份报告中表示，经过修剪的平均数据“现在也应该更接近目标一致的利率”。

“正如一系列广泛的指标所表明的那样，潜在通胀仍在向目标放缓的事实现在更加重要，因为沃什主席建议他进行分析通过考察广泛的指标来衡量通胀压力，”他补充道。 “我们预计市场将在未来几个月根据通胀数据定价加息，如果失业率如我们预测的那样上升，则定价下调。”

修剪后的平均通胀指标本质上就像一位老师对曲线测试进行评分：就达拉斯指标而言，它剔除了低端价格读数的 24% 和高端价格读数的 31%，以得出不存在通胀的更好中点。

该指标特别使用了个人消费支出价格指数——美联储的主要通胀预测工具——其结果于周四发布。美国商务部表示，本月所有商品指数下跌 0.1%，主要是由于燃料成本大幅下降，而排除食品和能源的核心指数上涨 0.1%。按年计算，这两个指标分别上涨了 3.7% 和 3.3%。

同样，克利夫兰联储的“16% 修剪平均值”包括低于 92% 和高于 8% 的价格变化。不过，该指标使用消费者价格指数作为基准。 6 月份，调整后的消费者物价指数 (CPI) 为 2.63%，在不四舍五入的基础上，为 2021 年 5 月以来的最低水平。

虽然这些措施可能会在 Warsh 领导下的美联储仪表板上占据更显着的位置，但也有一些警告。

首先，达拉斯联储主席洛里·洛根 (Lorie Logan) 负责监督其调整后的平均指标，他警告称，由于构成因素，不要对其过度解读。

具体来说，她说她的研究人员发现“价格上涨和下跌组合的变化正在导致修剪均值现在下降太多涨幅。这种效应可能使修剪均值低于真实的通胀趋势。”

洛根，事实上，本周反对联邦公开市场委员会保持基准利率稳定的决定，而是更愿意加息四分之一个百分点来解决五年多来一直高于目标的通胀问题。她在周五的一份声明中表示，“即使考虑到生产率的提高和暂时的供应冲击，通胀似乎仍趋向于 2% 左右，而不是一直达到 2%，而且风险仍在上升。”洛根的反对意见还包括明尼阿波利斯地区总统尼尔·卡什卡里和克利夫兰州州长贝丝·哈马克，两人都表示通胀高得令人不安，而美联储应该立即采取行动，而不是等待。

本周市场还关注总体通胀数据，以及美联储不加息的决定可能会加剧局势的看法。债券收益率飙升，尤其是在久期曲线的长端，投资者试图对未来的增长和通胀前景进行定价。

沃什本人以生产方面的一些潜在积极迹象为由，明确表示对当前通胀轨迹缺乏信心，但他坚称美联储仍有很多工作要做

“我的 FOMC 同事没有一个抱有任何幻想，”主席说。 “我们已经开始了新的篇章，我们明白，五年多来高于目标的通胀无法在九周内得到治愈，也无法通过一个月的小幅价格下跌来治愈。”

title: 伊朗战争导致油价上涨，埃克森美孚和雪佛龙利润大幅增长
content:
埃克森美孚和雪佛龙周五报告称，第二季度利润因伊朗战争导致油价上涨而大幅增长。

雪佛龙净利润飙升至120亿美元，与去年同期的25亿美元相比增长近400%。调整后每股收益为 6.06 美元，比华尔街的预期高出 50 美分。

首席执行官迈克·沃斯 (Mike Wirth) 对 CNBC 的贝基·奎克 (Becky Quick) 表示：“我们正在全力以赴，这很好，因为世界需要它。”

沃斯表示，在全球库存下降之际，中东石油供应面临的威胁已经扩大到霍尔木兹海峡以外。伊朗在也门的胡塞盟友已将冲突扩大到红海，红海已成为沙特阿拉伯石油出口的重要替代路线。

“局势面临压力，而且恐怕会继续如此，”沃斯告诉 CNBC。 “我们的时间不多了。时间一天天过去，情况变得更加困难。”

埃克森美孚公布的本季度利润为 145 亿美元，比去年同期的约 71 亿美元增加了一倍多。调整后每股收益为 3.52 美元，比分析师预期低 8 美分。

埃克森美孚首席执行官达伦·伍兹 (Darren Woods) 表示，业绩未达预期的原因是公司炼油业务遇到困难。他说，由于全球原油和产品市场的混乱，预测价格具有挑战性。

“我们遇到了太多的混乱，”伍兹告诉 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”节目。 “这尤其困难，特别是对于我们的炼油业务而言。很难预测我们将在该业务上采取什么价格。这就是失误的根源。”

雪佛龙股价上涨约 1%，而埃克森美孚股价下跌超过 2%。

以下是埃克森美孚和雪佛龙与 LSEG 调查的分析师的估计相比的情况：

美国4月至6月原油期货平均收盘价为每桶92.45美元，较第一季度上涨27%。

由于中东供应中断，出口激增，雪佛龙美国产量创下约200万桶/日的历史新高。全球产量达到 400 万桶/日，比去年同期的 340 万桶/日增长 20%。

埃克森美孚的上游产量达到 20 多年来的最高水平（不包括中东地区的中断）。德克萨斯州和新墨西哥州二叠纪盆地的产量创下历史新高。全球产量达到每天 450 万桶。

雪佛龙炼油业务利润跃升至 49 亿美元，比 2025 年第二季度的 7.37 亿美元增长 500%，原因是中东地区的混乱导致汽油和柴油价格飙升。

埃克森美孚炼油业务第二季度盈利 55 亿美元，扭转了亏损 1.3 美元的局面。由于墨西哥湾沿岸的强劲利用率和创纪录的柴油产量，第一季度的收入增长了 100 亿美元。该部门一年前的盈利总额为 14 亿美元。

雪佛龙第二季度生产业务的盈利增长 200%，达到 82 亿美元，而去年同期为 27 亿美元。埃克森美孚的上游勘探和生产利润为 79 亿美元，而 2025 年第二季度为 54 亿美元。

title: 通用汽车将于今年晚些时候推出自己的车载人工智能系统
content:
底特律——通用汽车计划在今年晚些时候推出更适合其客户的自己的车载人工智能系统。

通用汽车语音和人工智能/机器学习产品管理总监 Anna Santos 表示，与该公司最近推出的来自 Google 的 Gemini AI 助手相比，新的通用汽车人工智能助手预计将与车辆及其功能和远程信息处理信息更加集成。

“后来今年，我们将推出一款更深入集成的原生人工智能助手，它将对话式人工智能与通用汽车汽车知识和安吉星智能相结合，创造出超越通用助手所能做到的功能。

通用汽车去年宣布，今年将在数百万辆 2022 年款及更新车型上推出 Gemini 人工智能机器人，随后将推出通用汽车人工智能助手，但没有提供有关该技术的更多细节。

桑托斯表示，新通用汽车将推出该机器人。她拒绝透露助理的名字，她将能够更好地“了解车辆、驾驶和客户的需求，并使日常拥有变得更简单。”

有了 Gemini，客户可以自然地说话，而无需记住命令或重复上下文。它还开始提供“实时会话”，机器人将在其中进行对话或玩问答游戏或 20 个问题等游戏。它还可以控制通用汽车汽车的某些方面，例如温度和无线电控制，但一般来说就像通过手机一样操作。

“这对我们来说是更广泛的人工智能之旅的开始，”桑托斯说。 “只是位于车辆顶层的人工智能能做的事情是有限的。”

这家底特律汽车制造商正在与一家未透露姓名的大型语言模型提供商合作开发其技术，以协助通用汽车及其车主进行预测性维护、车辆遥测和其他更多以汽车为中心的功能。

这还可能包括诸如“儿童设置”之类的命令，可以为汽车量身定制音乐、座椅、加热/冷却和门锁控制。

“这些数据将归通用汽车所有，我们的目标是确保我们推出正确的技术，使我们能够建立我们希望能够带给人工智能助手的深厚的车辆专业知识，”桑托斯说。

title: 450,000 名被诈骗的学生贷款借款人有资格获得债务减免——以下是符合资格的人
content:
由于与美国教育部达成了 230 亿美元的集体诉讼和解协议，数十万学生贷款借款人的债务已被免除或很快就会被免除。

学生贷款借款人原告表示，他们的学校严重误导了他们，特朗普政府推迟了他们根据借款人辩护保护措施有权获得的救济。该计划允许受骗的联邦学生借款人免除债务。

7 月下旬，联邦上诉法院驳回了特朗普官员推迟对大量申请做出决定的最新请求，为另外近 20 万借款人取消学生贷款铺平了道路。这使得根据和解协议获得债务免除的借款人总数达到约 45 万。

法律挑战持续了三个总统任期，名称从 Sweet v. DeVos 改为 Sweet v. Cardona，再到 Sweet v. McMahon。倡导组织“掠夺性学生贷款项目”的总裁兼主任艾琳·康纳 (Eileen Connor) 表示，一名学生贷款借款人在等待教育部就其借款人辩护索赔做出决定时，她的债务从 25 万美元增加到大约 40 万美元。 PPSL 于 2019 年对特朗普政府提起诉讼。

康纳表示：“这清楚地表明，联邦政府不能简单地无视借款人的权利及其自身的法律义务而不承担任何后果。

教育部没有回应置评请求。

在 4 月份的法庭文件中，特朗普政府表示，需要时间来确定“数量出乎意料的大量”申请人的救济资格，这可能会导致“纳税人付出了巨额意外之财。”

数十所学校卷入斯威特和解协议，“教育部有大量机构不当行为的证据，”康纳说。许多学校（但不是全部）都是营利性机构，但现已关闭。

这些大学向学生贷款借款人做出了虚假承诺，包括他们的教育将带来稳定的职业、更高的收入和可转让的学分，她说：“相反，许多学校背负着巨额债务，雇主不尊重证书，学分无法转让，在某些情况下，根本没有学位。”

人们因联邦政府的原因而被拒绝抵押贷款和汽车融资。债务。康纳补充道，其他人推迟了家庭生活或推迟了医疗护理。

“借款人还描述了惊恐发作、焦虑、抑郁以及多年来无法规划未来的情况，”她说。

斯威特和解的资格取决于借款人就读的学校以及他们提交借款人辩护申请的时间，康纳说。她说：“这不是今天新获得的资格。”

如果您在 2022 年 11 月向教育部提出了一项待决索赔，您可能会被纳入和解类别。但该救济也适用于在 2019 年 12 月至 2020 年 10 月期间申请被拒绝的某些借款人。

您应该能够在 Studentaid.gov 上查看您的借款人辩护申请的提交时间。教育部还会通知符合资格的借款人。

高等教育专家马克·坎特罗维茨 (Mark Kantrowitz) 表示，该和解协议仅影响联邦学生贷款。

坎特罗维茨表示，“私人学生贷款不符合借款人辩护资格”，尽管近二十几个州维持着学费追偿基金计划，如果你就读的营利性学校已关闭。

根据和解协议清算的平均联邦学生贷款余额超过 48,000 美元，康纳说。她补充说：“然而，个人金额差异很大，许多借款人收到的金额或多或少都有所不同。”有资格获得和解的借款人也可能有资格获得之前为其债务支付的任何款项的退款。康纳说，符合条件的借款人的退款通常超过 15,000 美元。

借款人减免的截止日期还取决于其案件的详细信息以及他们申请贷款减免的时间。

康纳说，根据和解条款，教育部可以清除符合条件的借款人债务的最晚时间是 2027 年 6 月 15 日。在等待贷款减免期间，您无需付款。

title: 民主党人要求提供有关特朗普和卢特尼克家族与关键矿产交易的关系的信息
content:
周五，民主党参议员要求提供与联邦政府达成的十多项重要矿产交易的信息，这些交易可能有利于唐纳德·特朗普总统或商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克的家人。

参议员们表示，联邦政府正在与至少 14 家与特朗普或卢特尼克家族有经济关系的公司进行交易，并指出《纽约时报》6 月份的一项调查。据《泰晤士报》报道，特朗普政府已经或正在考虑向这些公司提供超过 89 亿美元的资金。

参议员们要求美国商务部、国防部、能源部、内政部和进出口银行保存与这些交易相关的所有记录和通信。

“尤其重要的是，旨在确保关键矿产等重要国家安全和经济利益的联邦投资应基于其优点，并决定花费纳税人的钱来获取这些资源。康涅狄格州参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔、加利福尼亚州亚当·希夫和马萨诸塞州伊丽莎白·沃伦在致各机构的信中表示：“这些交易的具体情况表明，这些目标可能不是政府在考虑这些交易时的首要考虑因素。”参议员们表示。

卢特尼克儿子经营的金融公司坎托·菲茨杰拉德 (Cantor Fitzgerald) 经常担任这些机构的顾问、承销商或配售代理。据《泰晤士报》报道，在另一封信中，参议员们援引 ProPublica 5 月份的一项调查，要求提供有关白宫参与五角大楼选择初创公司 Vulcan Elements 提供 6.2 亿美元贷款的信息。小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 的金融公司 1789 Capital 在交易之前投资了 Vulcan。

“这些报告引发了严重的道德和公共安全问题，并引发了人们的担忧：五角大楼正在腐败地根据与特朗普家族的关系优先为关键国防部件提供资金，”参议员们告诉五角大楼战略资本办公室主任戴维·洛尔奇。

白宫在回应评论请求时表示，“指导特朗普政府决策的唯一特殊利益是美国人民的最大利益。”

“保护和恢复美国关键供应链一直是总统的首要任务。特朗普和国务卿卢特尼克以及政府其他成员继续采取历史性行动，以维护美国的国家和经济安全。”白宫发言人库什·德赛说。
