title: 特朗普承诺农业将迎来“黄金时代”。爱荷华州的农民表示他们仍在等待
content:
IOWA — Farmer Aaron Lehman'shealth insurance premiumshave more than doubled since the start of the year, afterCongressdecided not to extend federal subsidies after they ended. As the Iran war drags on, thecost of diesel, fertilizer and other inputs he relies on to run his Polk City farm are up. Andcrop prices have been concerningly low.

Lehman grows soybeans, corn, oats and hay on the land his family has worked for five generations. The Lehmans and other Iowa farmers have endured difficult times, but 2026 — with all thevolatility around trade and foreign wars— feels different from recent years, Lehman said, despite PresidentDonald Trump's promises of a "golden age of American agriculture."

"Farmers are really tightening their belts," Lehman, president of theIowa Farmers Union, a nonpartisan organization that works to advance the causes of farmers and sustainable agriculture, told CNBC on his farm.

"It's one thing to say there's a golden age of agriculture right around the corner. Where?" Lehman said. "There's no indication that we're progressing towards healthier family farmers, that our rural communities are thriving under these policies."

Lehman is one of many farmers — normally areliably conservative group— voicing his concerns about the administration's policies and raising alarms about the direction of the agricultural economy in Iowa, as well as throughout much of the country.

The White House, in a statement to CNBC, pinned the blame on Trump's predecessor.

"Farmers suffered for years underJoe Biden, who increased the United States' trade deficit to over $1.2 trillion, raised input costs, and pushed woke DEI agricultural policies," White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said.

In addition to criticizing the Biden administration for not securing trade deals, which Trump said crippled the agricultural sector, the president has touted hisrollbacks of certain regulationsand the doubling of the so-called"death tax" exemption, which eases the financial burden on heirs when farmers pass down their equipment and acreage.

Trump also ordered his administration to distribute$12 billion in direct paymentsto farmersusing tariff revenue.In late June, the White House sent an$87.6 billion supplemental funding requestto Congress mostly to help pay for the Iran war but also including more than $10 billion in aid to farmers. The House in July approved a $95 billion budget package to help fund the war that includes $12 billion in farm aid.

But his tariff regime hasshut off marketsthat U.S. farmers rely on heavily. TheIran warhas put pressure on supply for necessities such as fuel and fertilizer and has at times sent prices soaring. Andinflationandhigh healthcare costshave only increased the pressure on farmers.

Amid these headwinds, approval of Trump has fallen to new lows among rural voters, according to aFox News pollreleased in July. That poll found just 44 percent of rural Americans approve of Trump, down 14 points from the same poll taken in June.

That's higher than Trump's40% approval ratingamong voters across the country, according to the CNBC All-America Economic Survey, released July 17, but down from60% approval among rural voters at the start of his second term.It's a potentially troubling development forRepublicansahead of the2026 midterms, in which they're trying to stave off aDemocraticwave and retain narrow majorities in the U.S. House and Senate.

At best, Trump's impact on farmers has been a mixed bag, according toChad Hart, an economics professor at Iowa State University.

Hart said the farm economy was already struggling at the beginning of the second Trump administration but that things have gotten worse and less predictable.

"I think farmers felt they had their pathway forward," Hart said, of the period at the start of Trump's latest term. "Change in policies meant we've seen more uncertainty there, and I think that has led to more concern for farmers as they're looking forward. Because right now they're not necessarily seeing where the endpoint is going to be with a lot of this."

Figures published by theAmerican Farm Bureau Federationin July paint a bleak picture.

High inflation, low commodity prices and volatile production costs are projected to lead to a $32 billion loss on major crops in 2027 for U.S. farmers, up from a $31 billion projected loss in 2026,the trade group reported.

In anApril survey, the group found 70% of U.S. farmers said they couldn't afford all the fertilizer they need.

Meanwhile, ajoint reportpublished this month by Iowa State University, the Iowa Farm Bureau and the Iowa Bankers Association found farm bankruptcies were up in 2025 and 2026 over those of the previous several years, both in Iowa and nationwide. The groups also reported that 19% of midsize and large Iowa farms they sampled were financially vulnerable in December 2025, more than double the number in 2022.

And more than a quarter of farmers, ranchers and agricultural managers rely on individual market health insurance, which is mainly composed of Affordable Care Act plans, according to ananalysis by the Kaiser Family Foundation. That means many, such as Lehman, could be facing higher premiums since the ACA subsidies expired in January, as most congressional Republicans refused to extend them.

Marc Short, who was White House director of legislative affairs in Trump's first term in office, wrote in a recentWashington Post op-edthat "President Trump's trade policies have punched farmers in the mouth."

Trump's tariffs on China, which led to retaliatory duties and aChinese pivot to other marketsfor products such as soybeans, have been particularly damaging, Short said in an interview with CNBC.

"In the first administration, we also assessed tariffs on China and there were repercussions for farmers. But I think there was a narrative that explained why China is our country's greatest threat," said Short, who was Vice PresidentMike Pence's chief of staff and is now board chair of Advancing American Freedom, the public policy organization Pence founded.

"I think the difference was there were alternative markets to go to. And right now a lot of farmers do not have alternative markets to go to because the trade war has been so indiscriminate," Short said.

Stress from the Trump administration's policies on farmers has not been evenly felt, according to Hart.Corn growers, he said, have been one relative exception.

"We didn't see a lot of response from our international customers when it came to retaliatory tariffs [on corn]," Hart said. "And right now, the corn market is actually experiencing one of the best years it's ever had in terms of moving quantities."

That may be in part because of high global consumerdemand for protein, Hart said. There's a huge need for corn and other crops traditionally used to feed livestock, he said, which has helped certain producers. According to theU.S. Department of Agriculture, corn growers produced 17 billion bushels in 2025, up from just under 15 billion the year prior.

"It's not necessarily that we're seeing the highest value of our corn exports, but when it comes to the number of bushels we're moving to the rest of the world, we're actually on a record pace right now," Hart said.

Some say the Trump administration's deregulatory bent has also been a boon to farmers. In the last year and a half, the White House has moved toboost domestic production of certain pesticides, and reduced regulations toexpand access to crop insurance, in addition to raising the estate tax exemption.

Jason Rogers, a corn, soybean and cattle farmer in Ottumwa who also runs a trucking business, said the deregulation helped but that more would be welcome.

Rogers acknowledged that times are tough for farmers now but said Trump inherited at least some of that situation.

"I think Biden created a lot of the problems that we have now. I think theObama administrationcreated a lot," Rogers said.

Rep.Zach Nunn, a GOP incumbent running for reelection in Iowa's 3rd Congressional District, said in an interview on Rogers' property that farmers are struggling and similarly pointed to Biden as a cause.

"I think we need to remember the fact that for the last four years under the Biden administration, we didn't have a single new trade deal for farmers. As a result, U.S. farmers lost $50 billion in global market share. That's unacceptable," said Nunn, citing afigure from the USDAunder Trump.

Nunn and Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, a Republican seeking reelection in Iowa's 1st Congressional District, also have touted the House's recentpassage of legislation to allow year-round sales of E15, an ethanol gasoline blend that's a boon to corn growers, as a positive sign for farmers in the Trump era.

But more than two months after it advanced out of the lower chamber, the legislation has not come up in the Senate. Lehman is skeptical it will.

"The E15 promise has been made many, many times, by multiple administrations. It has never garnered the support to get across the finish line," he said.

Short said he imagines the White House understands the complex situation farmers are finding themselves in. But he hasn't seen much effort to correct course, which he says could have political ramifications.

"I'm not witnessing policy changes," Short said, warning that could translate into risks for the GOP in November. "If there's a lack of enthusiasm among a core constituency, I think there's a huge risk to Republicans."

Lehman said farmers need more help from Washington.

title: 人工智能行业分裂，Meta 下跌近 9%，微软上涨 9%
content:
微软股价在盘前交易中上涨，而 Meta 因投资者对两家科技巨头的盈利给出不同的判断而下跌。

微软股价最近上涨 9%，而 Meta 下跌 9%。

周三，微软公布的第四财季收入超出了分析师预期，并报告其关键的 Azure 云业务增长了 43%，这也超出了市场预期。

该公司表示，现在已经其人工智能工作助手 Microsoft 365 Copilot 的付费席位从 4 月份的超过 2000 万增加到了超过 3000 万个，这进一步表明其部分人工智能投资正在获得回报。

“微软强劲的收入表现，加上 Copilot 的加速采用，表明其 1900 亿美元的数据中心建设正在开始带来回报，”Forrester 首席分析师 Tracy Woo 在一份报告中表示。周三。

尽管微软重申了 2026 年资本支出预测，并暗示 2027 财年可能会扩大支出，而此时市场对人工智能的成本感到紧张，但该公司的股价还是出现了上涨。

周三，该股在盘后交易中上涨了 8%，今年下跌了 24% 左右。

Meta 的情况则不同。这家社交媒体巨头未能达到投资者对本季度盈利和收入指引的预期。

Meta 表示，预计本季度收入在 610 亿美元至 640 亿美元之间，即该范围的中间值 625 亿美元。根据 LSEG 的数据，分析师预计指引为 631.5 亿美元。

与此同时，Meta 的自由现金流同比骤降 91%，至 7.84 亿美元，因为它继续在人工智能投资上投入资金。

Meta 的股价在周三的盘后交易中下跌，今年下跌了约 16%。

Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格表示，该公司“收到了很多报价”计算费用比公司支付的费用高得多”。如果 Meta 开始将多余的计算能力出租给第三方，这将是 Meta 方向的一个转变。然而，关于这项业务的细节很少。

与此同时，扎克伯格承认，公司需要保留计算资源来开发新产品。

Quilter Cheviot 技术研究主管本·巴林格 (Ben Barringer) 在周四的一份报告中表示：“目前，马克·扎克伯格的叙述对细节还不够了解，并且依赖于未来可以做的事情。”

“Meta 仍然有它在人工智能领域发挥着至关重要的作用，但它仍在寻找自己的发展方向，这就是为什么我们看到成本和收入看起来都有点不稳定。”

——CNBC 的 Jonathan Vanian 对本报告做出了贡献。

title: 伊朗战争推高石油和天然气价格，壳牌公布四年来最佳季度利润
content:
英国能源巨头谢隆公司周四公布的第二季度利润强于预期，受益于不断蔓延的中东冲突期间石油和天然气价格的上涨。

根据伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 编制的共识，这家石油巨头公布 4 月至 6 月期间调整后收益为 98.4 亿美元，轻松超过分析师预期的 87.9 亿美元。公司提供的另一份分析师预测显示，壳牌第二季度的预期利润为 89.2 亿美元。

壳牌公布的去年同期调整后收益为 42.6 亿美元，2026 年前三个月为 69.2 亿美元。

这标志着壳牌自 2022 年第二季度以来的最佳季度业绩，当时该公司公布的石油和天然气价格收益为 114.7 亿美元俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰后，石油价格飙升。

“波动性是新常态，”壳牌首席执行官 Wael Sawan 周四在 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目中表示。

“我们一直在努力建立的是一家能够在波动中蓬勃发展的公司。所以，你说得完全正确，当然，宏观经济形势使得大宗商品价格很高，这为我们的业绩提供了非常强大的推动力，”Sawan

“但我们可以控制两个关键要素，我们将继续非常非常好地提供这些要素。一是出色的运营业绩，你可以在我们的每一项业务中看到这一点，这本身就支撑了第二点。当然，第二是非常强大的交易和优化，”他补充道。

壳牌表示，它将在下个季度维持 30 亿美元的股票回购计划步伐。

这一丰硕成果来自于能源巨头。伊朗战争期间化石燃料价格飙升，使该公司的利润得到提升。

美国周三对中东发动了自上周暂停轰炸行动以来的首次空袭。美国中央司令部称此次袭击是对伊朗周二企图袭击中东美军的“有力回应”。

伦敦上市的壳牌股票周四上午上涨 1.5%。今年迄今为止，该公司股价已上涨约 21%，尽管该公司落后于英国英国石油公司 (BP) 和法国道达尔能源公司 (TotalEnergies) 以及美国石油巨头埃克森美孚 (Exxon Mobiland) 和雪佛龙 (Chevron) 等公司。

title: OpenAI 黑客事件后特朗普考虑控制人工智能
content: 图片来源，EPA图片说明，特朗普政府对人工智能采取了更加放手的态度。作者：Kali HaysTechnology记者发布2026年7月30日，英国夏令时间01:41更新于32分钟前美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三表示，在最近的网络安全事件后，他的政府正在考虑对人工智能工具行使更多权力。当被问及OpenAI的工具是否不当破坏其他公司的私有技术时，特朗普表示表示：“我们正在关注人工智能，我们正在关注控制，我们也在确保我们的领先地位。”这标志着他的政府基调的变化，对这项技术采取了更加不干涉的态度。特朗普发表此番言论之前，不仅流行人工智能工具的明显黑客能力升级，而且白宫针对中国竞争技术的威胁也在升级。特朗普补充说，虽然对人工智能工具的某种控制已经摆在桌面上，但这样的举动必须谨慎行事。特朗普补充道：“中国几乎没有对人工智能进行控制，它有点随心所欲。”我们已联系白宫征求更多评论。 BBC 还联系了中国驻华盛顿大使馆请其置评。上周，OpenAI 已对至少两起涉及其人工智能工具超出其设计和指示范围的黑客事件负责。在周三前往华盛顿期间，OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 被记者问及是否还有更多系统被该公司的工具攻破。奥尔特曼说：“我的意思是，可能会有。” OpenAI 的主要美国竞争对手决定向公众发布一个模型，该模型此前曾表示该模型风险太大，无法广泛使用。 与此同时，在 4 月份的一份白宫内部备忘录中，特朗普的高级技术顾问 Michael Kratsios 指责中国的人工智能公司“工业规模”窃取美国人工智能技术。他上周再次这样做，声称中国Moonshot AI流行的Kimi 3人工智能模型是通过窃取Anthropic的信息而开发的。中国政府一直否认此类指控。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也警告说，中国人工智能公司可能因此类活动而面临制裁。美国联邦通信委员会本周禁止进口新的外国制造的人形机器人。中国正在开发的大多数人工智能模型都是开源的，这意味着它们在构建后可以在网上免费提供给任何拥有适当计算机设备的人下载和使用。最近，美国大多数主要科技公司的高管都签署了支持开源模型的公开声明，外部。黑客？发表于 4 天前 OpenAI 称其流氓人工智能试图攻击其他公司发布于 23 小时前 OpenAI 表示其人工智能变得流氓并发起了“前所未有的”网络攻击发布于 7 月 22 日

title: 伊朗战争导致油价上涨，壳牌利润翻倍
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者Jennifer Meierhans商业记者发布2026年7月30日，英国夏令时间08:00英国标准时间43分钟前更新在伊朗战争推高油价后，壳牌今年第二季度的利润翻了一番多。这家石油巨头4月至6月期间的利润达到98.4亿美元（73.7亿英镑）——高于去年同期的42.6亿美元自美以与伊朗爆发战争以来，由于通过霍尔木兹海峡的全球石油和液化天然气（LNG）供应受到严重干扰，石油价格飙升。壳牌首席执行官瓦埃尔·萨万（Wael Sawan）表示，该公司“在全球能源市场严重混乱的又一个季度中，经营业绩取得了非常强劲的业绩”。加上今年前三个月的利润69.2亿美元，这意味着壳牌上半年的利润猛增了70%壳牌以及英国石油公司和挪威国家石油公司等其他能源巨头今年都获得了丰厚的利润，部分原因在于油价波动的交易。在冲突开始之前，全球油价基准布伦特原油的价格约为每桶73美元。此后，它曾达到120美元以上的峰值，但由于霍尔木兹海峡何时重新开放的猜测，油价又回落至100美元以下。油价的这些大幅波动可能会扩大差距买卖价格之间的差异通常使交易者能够赚取更大的利润。相关主题壳牌公司石油和天然气行业石油

title: 美联储维持利率稳定后，美国国债继续遭到抛售
content:
美国周四，随着投资者权衡美联储维持利率稳定的决定，并寻求对未来货币政策决策的洞察，美国国债收益率继续攀升。

美国东部时间凌晨 3:20，30 年期国债收益率在周三触及 2007 年 7 月以来的最高水平后，已上涨超过 9 个基点至 5.236%。基准10年期国债收益率飙升逾8个基点至4.7%，2年期国债收益率上涨5个基点至4.289%。

1个基点等于0.01%，收益率和价格走势相反。

周三，美联储投票决定在9-3年的政策中将关键利率稳定在3.5%至3.75%的区间。联邦公开市场委员会 (FOMC) 主席凯文·沃什 (Kevin Warsh) 主持的第二次会议上投票。

联邦公开市场委员会 (FOMC) 在决定后发表声明称，“尽管不确定性上升，但经济活动仍在稳步扩张，部分原因是中东冲突。”

“就业增长与劳动力同步增长，失业率几乎没有变化。”

德意志银行分析师还指出，国债抛售隔夜仍在继续，并表示其经济学家仍在继续抛售国债。预计美联储今年将加息 50 个基点，这意味着 9 月和 12 月加息 25 个基点。

“但他们认为 FOMC 不太可能对昨天的市场反应感到太大安慰，长期利率上升，加上远期实际收益率下降，表明人们对价格稳定即将恢复的怀疑，”分析师表示。

他们补充说，美国整体信贷状况仍然具有支撑性，但更陡峭的收益率曲线可能会增加压力疲软的房地产市场。

投资者还将等待周四公布的每周初请失业金人数和 6 月份个人消费支出价格指数。

道琼斯估计，总体通胀率预计将每年增长 3.7%，核心通胀率（不包括食品和能源价格）将上涨 3.3%。

title: 美国在突然导弹袭击后袭击伊朗，使缓和局势的希望破灭
content:
美国军队周三在美国境内完成了对伊朗的“猛烈”打击，以报复伊朗对该地区美军的导弹袭击，短暂停顿后引发了冲突升级的担忧。

美国中央司令部称此次行动是对伊朗周二企图袭击中东美军的“有力回应”。

中央司令部表示，在长达两个小时的袭击中，美国袭击了伊朗各地的数十个伊斯兰革命卫队目标，包括军事指挥中心、导弹和无人机设施、沿海监视和防御站点以及海上能力。

这次袭击旨在进一步削弱伊朗及其代理人对美国军队、商业航运和军事设施的威胁。伊朗军队周二晚些时候在美国本土向海湾地区的美军发射了多枚弹道导弹，尽管所有导弹均被拦截，随后发起了新的袭击。约旦武装部队表示，该国防空系统拦截了从伊朗发射的五枚导弹。

安全公司全球卫士副总裁、退役美国陆军上校赛斯·克鲁姆里奇表示，周二的突然袭击打破了伊朗对美国袭击的反应模式，表明德黑兰愿意重启敌对行动。

此举表明伊朗打算“对美国未来的军事行动做出更积极的反应，并可能会撤离”来自外交，”克鲁姆里奇说。他说，包括机场、电网、海水淡化厂和海湾能源设施在内的关键民用基础设施可能再次成为攻击目标。

联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷森周三警告称，长期冲突有可能波及更广泛的地区。

罢工的恢复标志着冲突的最新转折，自二月底爆发战斗以来，这场冲突已严重冲击石油市场，并扰乱了霍尔木兹海峡的航运。上周末，美国已停止对伊朗目标进行两周的射击，外交官试图给和谈“一些空间”。

特朗普几小时前电报了报复行动，警告下令对伊朗进行猛烈打击。周三早些时候，特朗普对福克斯新闻记者表示：“我们将严厉打击他们。他们将受到打击。”特朗普的言论导致布伦特原油期货周三上涨 7.9%，收于每桶 90.74 美元，而美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨 6.6%，收于每桶 84.46 美元。周四亚洲交易中油价小幅走低。

整个地区的敌对行动有所扩大。美国和沙特阿拉伯武装部队周二对伊拉克境内与伊朗结盟的民兵发动联合打击，这些民兵的目标是利雅得和沙特阿拉伯东部地区的石油设施。也门胡塞武装声称袭击了沙特延布红海出口码头的管道基础设施。

以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在白宫会见特朗普，就伊朗战争问题举行了“富有成效的”90分钟会议。

特朗普周三还要求立法者修改俄罗斯制裁法案，授权他对伊朗征收关税。据《国会山报》报道，他在椭圆形办公室对记者表示：“我希望他们将伊朗列为关税，而不仅仅是制裁。” 2025 年，美国与伊朗的货物贸易额仅为 6000 万美元。

不断升级的紧张局势给“波斯湾迅速缓和紧张局势的想法泼了一盆冷水”，并使重启谈判的希望变得渺茫，荷兰国际银行 (ING Bank) 大宗商品策略主管沃伦·帕特森 (Warren Patterson) 表示。

帕特森表示，针对沙特石油基础设施的攻击增加了长期供应中断的风险，援引报道称，周末胡塞武装袭击后，该国每天生产 40 万桶的吉赞炼油厂已关闭。

通过霍尔木兹海峡的油轮运输实际上已经停止。伊朗拒绝了阿曼关于平均分配关键干道航运控制权的提议，要求做出一项安排，使其对入境交通进行全面监督，对出境通道进行部分监督。

帕特森表示，石油卡特尔OPEC+预计将在8月2日的会议上宣布9月供应量增加188,000桶/日，完成每日165万桶的自愿减产。一旦中断现象消失，供应的增加就会强化市场到 2027 年供应充足的观点。

title: 霍尔木兹海峡只是面临新海战时代的贸易咽喉要地
content:
The Strait of Hormuz is rattling global trade, but the waterway is just one example of a vital maritime corridor becoming a frontline, in a new age of drones and missiles targeting economic lifelines.

From the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea to the Black Sea,attackson commercial vessels have disrupted trade, raised insurance and freight costs, and forced shipping companies to reconsider routes once treated as dependable.

The stakes are high: roughly 80% of global merchandise trade by volume moves by sea. Disrupting even one major route can delay cargo, tighten supplies and drive up prices for energy, food and consumer goods thousands of miles away.

"We have a new chokepoint and a new war," David Roche, president and global strategist at Quantum Strategy, wrote in a July report, referring to theSea of Azov, where Ukrainian drones have been striking Russian tankers, and the Black Sea.

Roche described this fighting as the first maritime offensive conducted almost entirely with drones, supplemented by missiles. Such weapons give smaller military forces a cheaper means of threatening ships, ports and other infrastructure whose disruption carries a huge economic cost.

Quantum estimates that about 25% of Russia's grain exports and 25% to 30% of its Black Sea oil exports could be disrupted. Russia grows more than a fifth of internationally traded wheat, magnifying the potential consequences for global food prices.

Yevgeniya Gaber, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank, said Russia's move earlier this month to suspend shipping through the Kerch Strait, which connects the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea, has effectively shut down a vital maritime corridor.

"Maritime transport through the Sea of Azov had become an increasingly important alternative to the land corridor connecting Russia with occupied Crimea," Gaber told CNBC by email.

"The economic implications are equally important," Gaber said, adding that the Sea of Azov has been used not only to transport sanctioned crude oil and petroleum products but also grain, coal and steel.

Gaber said Ukraine'seffortsto exploit Russia's maritime and economic weaknesses constitute "one of the most significant blows to military and commercial fleets" since World War II. Indeed, Ukraine says it has degraded roughly one-third of Russia's Black Sea fleet since 2022.

In the Strait of Hormuz, commercial operators are contending with attacks and rapidly shifting signals over whether passage is safe. Governments can declare a waterway open, but shipowners make their own decisions based on the likelihood of a vessel being hit and crew members being injured or killed.

"We often treat the Strait of Hormuz, the Black Sea, or Bab el-Mandeb as isolated events. They are not," said Daejin Lee, global head of research at Fertistream Freight.

"These waterways are increasingly becoming battlegrounds within the broader transition toward a new world order," he told CNBC via email.

And the next threats are already emerging.

"If you're talking about the next flashpoint, I wouldn't look at the Strait of Hormuz," said Lars Jensen, chief executive officer of Vespucci Maritime. "I would look at the Panama Canal."

The strategic passage, which has offered a shortcut for ships transiting between the Pacific and the North Atlantic for more than a century, is already caught in ageopolitical disputeinvolving the U.S., China and Panama over influence. Potential weather-related restrictions toward the end of this year and early next year could compound those tensions by reducing capacity, Jensen added.

For shipping companies, the challenge is preparing for a world where the next chokepoint can emerge before the last one has reopened.

Kevin O'Marah, co-founder and chief research officer at supply chain intelligence firm Zero100, told CNBC the Strait of Hormuz became the most critical part of the U.S.-Iran war after Iran discovered merely threatening traffic there was enough to stop it.

While none of Zero100's clients had come under attack in the strait, O'Marah said some had decided to avoid that risk by actively managing inventories and rerouting shipments.

"It has added cost and delay for some of our clients in the energy, food, and electronics industries," he said.

"As of now, traffic through the Strait looks to be running at about half the normal flow. The recent breakdown in the ceasefire has definitely hurt the situation but no one is surprised. Supply chain leaders, and in particular logistics specialists like Martin Brower and Maersk, are aware and have well established protocols for dealing with the risk."

Mitigation strategies include rerouting across the Arabian Peninsula via pipeline for oil, overland into Turkey for certain kinds of commodities and avoiding the area completely as much as possible, O'Marah said.

The war in the Middle East "does not look like an escalating conflict to most supply chain leaders, but it does look likely to be a long-term problem in terms of freedom of movement through the Strait of Hormuz," he added.

"We are planning on a steady state of transportation uncertainty and costs associated with reroutings, inventory buffering, and shipping surcharges."

Alain Bejjani, a Dubai-based investor, business executive and judge on "Shark Tank Lebanon," told CNBC shipping lanes would stay at the center of the war "because they are the conflict."

"The war has migrated from territory to logistics. A strait does not close when missiles fly; it closes when insurers stop writing cover," he said. "That makes disruption cheap to sustain and hard to price, which is exactly why it persists."

A spokesperson for insurance broker Gallagher told CNBC war risk insurance — an add-on that covers financial losses caused by war, terrorism, and civil unrest — is still available. But they noted that "a handful but not many" ship owners or charters are opting to travel through the Strait of Hormuz.

"Given the challenging maritime security environment, rates have increased from levels that owners and charterers will be used to. The cost will vary depending on the vessel type, cargo and routing, however marine insurers are continuing to provide cover and helping to ensure marine commerce can continue with adequate coverage in place," they added.

Bejjani told CNBC that the structural consequence of maritime warfare "is bigger than most people realize."

"The Gulf is bracketed by two straits, not one, and the region is now designing around both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb to the maximum extent possible," he said.

"That is new. Past crises produced hedges. This one is producing an architecture: overland corridors, bypass pipelines, forward storage near the markets that matter most. It will cost heavily, take a decade, and ripple for decades more. I expect other strait-dependent regions to follow, though few with the same urgency or resources."

He warned that, although shipping will maintain its edge in terms of volumes, it is likely to "lose its monopoly on trust" in the business world.

"Other modes of transport will be substantially enhanced where certainty matters most, and redundancy becomes a permanent, priced feature of logistics," he said.

"The strait will reopen. The assumption that it stays open for free will not return."

title: 这就是为什么欧洲炎热的夏季正在成为一项代价高昂的挑战
content:
Europe's increasingly extreme summers are becoming an economic problem, with more frequent heatwaves driving up costs, disrupting businesses and weighing on growth.

Huge wildfireshave been raging in France and Spain, burning 300,000 acres and forcing the evacuation of 300,000 people.The scenes echo last year's Los Angeles wildfires, when blazes overwhelmed firefighting resources, triggered mass evacuations and destroyed thousands of homes.

AWorld Meteorological Organization(WMO) report looking at Europe in 2025 noted the continent had "seen increased wildfire potential ... with a growing number of larger fires and an extended fire season. Western Europe recorded its hottest June ever this year, per the WMO.

French ‌Finance Minister Roland Lescure ‌said on Monday that the latest wildfires were "like a clap of thunder" for the local economy.

But the fires are part of a broader economic strain across health care, cooling, transportation, agriculture, insurance and public budgets, caused by rising temperatures. Economists have also warned that repeated heatwaves — Western Europe is facing its third in six weeks — can drag on output by reducing productivity, disrupting supply chains, depressing tourism and pushing up food prices, turning summer weather into a recurring macroeconomic risk.

"This is really a big economic challenge," Georg Zachmann, a senior fellow at Bruegel, specializing in energy and climate policies, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday.

"We need really to do everything we can do to make sure that our systems are adapted early on, as much as possible, and the speed of climate change is slowed down as much as possible, so that we don't get into a situation where our absorptive capacity for such risks is not exceeded," Zachmann told CNBC'sRitika Gupta.

The increased intensity and frequency of extreme weather means Europe has to deal with the cost of cooling, healthcare, emergency infrastructure, transportation, and agriculture, ING's Global Head of Macro Carsten Brzeski said in a report in June.

"The uncomfortable truth is that heatwaves have quietly graduated from 'weather event' to 'macro variable,'" Brzeski said.

Heatwaves, droughts and floods during the summer of 2025 caused the European economy to lose some 0.3% of output, and the damage could grow to an accumulated 0.8% by 2029, due to lost productivity, supply chain disruption, and depressed tourism revenue, a 2025 joint paper from the University of Mannheim and the European Central Bank found.

Additionally,agricultural commoditiessuch as cocoa, coffee and wheat are expected to be among the hardest-hit asset classes from the heatwave, as warmer and more volatile weather threatens crop yields and drives up food prices.

Meanwhile, extreme weather events such as Europe's wildfires are likely to impact countries' fiscal budgets, Zachmann said, as they pay for evacuations, firefighting, and infrastructure recovery.

"Just to give you one example,the 2025 fires in Californiamight have cost some 40 to 60 billion in direct cost, and the indirect costs have been estimated to some 300 billion. So it's really a big thing," he added.

Zachmann said that disasters that strike at a random pattern cause inflation. "The prices substantially increase. The risk premium increases for people that want to build there in the future."

Insurance companies also paid out $56.3 billion in losses for wildfires in the 2010s, six times more than the $8.7 billion they paid in the 2000s, areport from Allianz Commercialnoted in June. The sectors hardest hit include utility and energy, real estate, construction, agriculture, and transportation.

ING's Brzeski told CNBC a "bittersweet consequence" of the wildfires in France and Spain is that it likely will also lead to positive economic activity once the reconstruction begins, in common with other natural disasters.

With a heatwave underway in the region, experts have warned that it could exacerbate the fires.

Stefan Doerr, a professor of wildland fire science at Swansea University, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday that climate change and poor landscape management are playing a "major role" in contributing to the wildfires.

Doerr said decades of agricultural land abandonment and centuries of human-shaped landscapes have left parts of southern Europe with dense, highly flammable vegetation that is more vulnerable to wildfires during extreme heat and drought.

"If we had a natural landscape, we would have actually, in some places, at least far less flammable forests," he said. "This is man-made. It's not that the plants are not natural, but the way the landscape looks now is entirely artificial."

title: 中国威胁对美国仿人机器人禁令进行报复，称其“严重损害”两国关系
content:
BEIJING — The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has repeatedly ignored Beijing's restrained stance on product bans, China's commerce ministry said Thursday, threatening retaliation.

The FCC on Tuesday said due to cybersecurity concerns, it added foreign-made advanced robotic devices,including humanoids, to a list restricting imports to the U.S.The statementdid not specify a country, and said retailers could still import models the FCC has previously approved.

As the FCC keeps escalating restrictions on Chinese goods, it "severely damages China-U.S. economic and trade stability," China's commerce ministry said in an online statement Thursday. That's according to a CNBC translation of Mandarin.

The ministry urged the U.S. to withdraw the decision, and threatened countermeasures if it failed to do so.

"This is bad news for Chinese humanoid producers planning their IPOs in the coming months," said Marc Einstein, a research director at Counterpoint Research. "The two major cards China can play are to further restrict rare earth sales to American companies and further restricting Chinese market access for American companies likeTeslaandNVIDIA."

The commerce ministry's statement comes as U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to host Chinese President Xi Jinping in September. Tensions over the tech race have meanwhile intensified, with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent saying the U.S. couldsanction China over AI model "theft."

Trump on Thursday indicated in public comments that theU.S. might take a more cautious stance on AI controlsin order to maintain American tech leadership over China.

Chinese companies Agibot, Unitree and UBTech accounted for the top-three humanoid companies by installation market share last year, according to Counterpoint. Tesla's Optimus ranked fifth.

Hong Kong-listed UBTech shares briefly fell more than 6% in Thursday morning trading. Unitree and Agibot have filed to go public.

Robostore, a distributor of Chinese humanoid robots in North America, has been preparing by expanding its U.S.-based capabilities, CEO Teddy Haggerty said in a statement to CNBC. He did not elaborate on details.

—CNBC's Matthew Tan contributed to this report.

title: 分析：维持利率不变后，美联储主席沃什的可信度受到质疑
content:
For a Federal Reserve chairman who prizes credibility above all other virtues, the market's reaction toKevin Warsh'sremarks Wednesday must have been painful.

Warsh hosted a press conference Wednesday afternoon following a meeting of theFederal Open Market Committee, whichvoted 9-3 to leave interest rates unchanged. It was just the second such meeting since Warsh became head of the Fed on May 22. Investors responded by sharply lowering the chances that the Fed will raise interest rates at its next meeting but also raised the yields on long-term government debt.

After the press conference, the yield on the30-year Treasuryhit itshighest level since 2007, while the yield on the 2-year Treasury fell. The chances that the Fed would leave interest rates unchanged at its next meeting jumped by 20 percentage points to 45%,according to CME FedWatch.

That dynamic suggests investors believe the Fed won't act immediately oninflation readingsthat by Warsh's account have been above the Fed's 2% target for at least 63 months, and that it may have to act on more aggressively later as the economy heats up for the long haul.

Before taking the job, Warshsharply criticized his predecessorJerome Powell when long-term Treasury interest rates moved up after the Fed cut the federal funds rate and said repeatedly that the underlying problem was Powell's lack of credibility. The situation Wednesday was slightly different, in that the Fed didn't cut interest rates but held them steady. Warsh also suggested Wednesday that recent rises in long-term interest rates may have reflected positive economic news, such as strong business investment.

Still, few in the markets saw it that way.

Warsh needed to articulate what it would take for him to want to eventually raise interest rates in the face of stubborn inflation, Jon Hilsenrath, a longtime Fed watcher, wrote in a note to clients after Warsh's press conference.

"Warsh didn't convey the message clearly or explicitly, and the bond market puked on him," Hilsenrath wrote.

Warsh declined to answer reporters' questions about the details of why he, along with eight others on the FOMC, deemed the interest rate was in the right place at 3.5-3.75%, where it has been for months. Warsh has shifted Fed policy by ending a practice known asforward guidance. Past Fed chairs would strongly signal where they expected interest rates to go in the future. Warsh believes forward guidance made the Fed inflexible and obscured signals from the markets. As a result, he doesn't talk much about how he makes decisions.

"I understand the desire for rolling forecasts and commentary from this committee, but for our part, we need to observe market reaction to developments, direct and unfiltered," Warsh said in his opening remarks Wednesday.

The press conference that followed left some economists baffled.

"I thought today's press conference was confusing and often internally contradictory," Eric Winograd, chief U.S. economist for AllianceBernstein, wrote to clients.

Consumer-price-index data showedprices declining by 0.4% in June, offering an opportunity for the chairman to seize on some positive economic data. But Warsh said that factor was "not much" of a consideration for him, while affirming inflation was still "elevated."

The Fed is officially committed to achieving 2% annual inflation over the long run in an alternative measure of inflation, the personal consumption expenditures index. Warsh wasn't much clearer on whether he was happy with that data either, which was at4.1% in itsmost recent reading, and added that one of the five task forces he has appointed to reviewreforms at the Fedmight want to downplay PCE as the central bank's official target when it issues its report at the end of the year.

We are sticking with PCE for now, Warsh said. But, "who knows, come after next January, what we might say about strategy."

Warsh's unwillingness to say exactly what might move him to raise interest rates, combined with his suggestion that he wasn't committed to the Fed's reliance on PCE, had some in the markets re-evaluating his brief tenure.

"Both of these points raise questions about the new chair's credibility in delivering lower inflation," wrote Michael Feroli, chief U.S. economist at JPMorgan Chase.

The Fed chairman doesn't set interest rates alone. He is one of a dozen votes on the FOMC.Three voters dissentedfrom Wednesday's decision to keep interest rates steady. If economic data doesn't improve rapidly in the next few months, more may join them.

"We believe this will add some urgency for the rest of the committee to act on its mandate," Feroli wrote. A Fed chair has never been in the minority on a vote about interest rates.

That leaves Warsh in a difficult place, with his credibility potentially eroded in the face of the markets and within the Fed itself just months into the job.

title: SpaceX 面临众议院能源委员会要求参观其位于孟菲斯的人工智能数据中心
content:
众议院能源和商业委员会的最高民主党人要求 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 参观其公司位于田纳西州孟菲斯市及其周边地区的 xAI 数据中心和发电厂。

“美国人担心数据中心和大型科技公司推动更多人工智能对他们的社区、就业、财产价值和未来意味着什么，”众议员弗兰克·帕隆 (D-NJ) 在周三给马斯克的信中写道。 “电价飞涨，电网紧张，我们清洁的空气和水受到污染，噪音正在侵蚀社区的健康和耐心。”

在 xAI 在孟菲斯建设数据中心以及 OpenAI、Meta、微软和谷歌的其他项目正在进行之后，美国公众对数据中心的反对情绪日益高涨。盖洛普在 5 月份发布的一项调查中发现，十分之七的美国人反对在孟菲斯建设人工智能数据中心。 48% 的人强烈反对。

Pallone 要求在 8 月 11 日之前提供有关马斯克设施的信息。

SpaceX 没有回应置评请求。

SpaceX 的人工智能设施（称为 Colossus 和 Colossus 2）包括三个配备了尖端 Nvidia 处理器的数据中心。它们是在 SpaceX 收购 Musk 的初创公司之前建造的，该公司是 Grok 的人工智能模型、聊天机器人和图像编辑工具的开发商。

这些设施是 SpaceX 人工智能雄心的核心，因为该公司试图与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等公司竞争，并最终建立轨道数据中心。

Pallone 谴责 SpaceX 和马斯克“无视当地社区的健康和福祉”。他表示，该公司通过“卡车运输离网燃气轮机”为设施供电，给邻居造成了“巨大的健康风险”，而所有这些都没有适当的许可和污染控制。

特朗普总统的司法部已提出动议进行干预，并有效帮助 xAI 击退环境倡导者和密西西比州全国有色人种协进会提起的诉讼，以阻止该公司使用涉嫌非法的空气污染物质

“特朗普政府基本上声称，它独自决定 SpaceXAI 和其他公司是否能获得不受阻碍地污染污染的免费通行证，”帕隆写道。 “但仅仅因为特朗普政府会竭尽全力让科技公司自由支配社区的空气、水和土地，并不意味着你的行为就合法。”

新泽西州州长、民主党人米基·谢里尔(Mikie Sherrill)本月早些时候颁布了立法，以确保数据中心运营商支付公平的电费，而不是将成本转嫁到居民和企业身上。

title: 美国希望亚洲使用其人工智能——但中国在更便宜的型号上占据主导地位
content:
BEIJING — The artificial intelligence race between the U.S. and China is heating up in the world's largest continent: Asia.

"The American strategy is to stop China from becoming the leading AI supplier for the rest of Asia ... and frankly the whole world," said Gary Dvorchak, managing director at The Blueshirt Group. While China's alternatives are cheaper, he pointed out the U.S. currently offers a more complete solution from chips to AI models.

But the U.S. sales challenge was apparent at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation "Digital Weeks" in the southwestern Chinese city of Chengdu this month.

The U.S. leftfew public tracesof its involvement in the event, despitea U.S. officialand aU.S. business representative to APECboth highlighting AI in promoting the Chengdu event earlier this year. The subdued U.S. presence comes after Anthropic flip-flopped on its Fable AI model releasedue to abrupt U.S. policy changes, andnew Chinese AI modelshave recently launched similar capabilities for far less.

In contrast, last summer at the first APEC AI meeting in South Korea, Michael Kratsios, President Donald Trump's chief science and technology policy advisor, highlighted the U.S. AI Action Plan and the establishment of the American AI Exports Program, according to aWhite House transcript of his remarks.

However, earlier this month Politico cited three former officials in reporting the Commerce Department has so farreceived a less-than-expected 78 applicationsfor the American AI Exports Program.

And on July 24 at an APEC High-level Forum on AI organized by China's cybersecurity regulator, Bill Guidera, deputy under secretary for innovation and engagement at the U.S. Department of Commerce, still focused on the AI exports program, according to materials reviewed by CNBC.

He called broadly for Asia-Pacific partnerships, noting buyers can acquire a full U.S. tech stack or just portions through the exports program. "It is the brilliant design that shows the strength, security and capability of U.S. AI," Guidera said.

The Commerce Department's International Trade Administration confirmed in aJuly 29 social media postthat Guidera spoke in Chengdu. When asked about the Politico report, an ITA spokesperson said the volume of applications "exceeded our expectations." The White House did not respond to a CNBC request for comment.

American business showcases were also limited. Google and Meta were the only U.S. companies that CNBC noted had booths at APEC as of July 23, among booths for Thailand and China, which were mostly Chengdu-based companies. The two U.S. companies respectively emphasized molecular AI system AlphaFold and AI applications for small businesses, rather than large language models.

Google's government affairs vice president, Wilson L. White, only made passing references to Gemini in a speech on July 24, whileTencentVice President Cai Guangzhong took the stage after White to emphasize growing adoption of its Hunyuan LLM and a cloud project in Thailand.

China is hosting APEC this year, which comes at a critical moment ofU.S.-China tensions and tech rivalry.

Beijing has doubled down on the opportunity to emphasize its AI capabilities, which are mostly open-source versus largely closed U.S. models.

Chinese President Xi Jinping announced at the World AI Conference in Shanghai on July 17 that China wouldprovide developing countrieswith 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminars, while developing AI application cooperation centers withSoutheast Asia and other regions.

Beijing then sent a high-ranking official, Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, to advocate for developing tech standards with other Asia Pacific nations at the minister-level APEC Digital Weeks on July 23. Later that day, the 21 member economies, including the U.S.,agreed to back open-source AIwith "strong security."

"The 'endorsement' of open-source models with strong security assurance gives China's open-weight strategy greater regional legitimacy, especially across emerging Asian economies where deployment cost and technological sovereignty are major considerations," said Wei Sun, principal analyst, artificial intelligence, Counterpoint Research.

But rather than a world divided into spheres of U.S. and Chinese AI, Sun expects a combination of the tech, especially in Asia.

With more than1,300 living languages in Southeast Asiaalone, just using a U.S. or Chinese AI model isn't as straightforward as it looks.

Governments in Asia and elsewhere are spending "billions" on AI systems tailored to local languages, according to privately funded startup Votee AI. CEO Pak-Sun Ting said he is working with at least five governments, including two in Southeast Asia, and that the startup is already making well over $10 million in revenue a year.

Ting said entities in Southeast Asia tend to use Nvidia chips, especially for AI training, but may use other chips for running models. He noted Votee'sopen-source model for Cantonese speakerswas developed partly using Alibaba's open-source Qwen model.

AI's ability to generate economic returns remains critical regardless of origin.

"While the U.S. and China are fiercely competing in AI technology and diplomacy through distinct approaches, they ultimately cannot fully decouple from one another," said Yue Su, principal economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit.

She pointed out the light U.S. presence at APEC wasn't that surprising given other events, such as a San Francisco AI Summit on July 24.

South Korea's tech ministryorganized the event, where President Lee Jae-myung sought to build onKorean chip and AI megaprojectsbymeeting with U.S. frontier AI model leadersSam Altman of OpenAI, Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Jensen Huang of Nvidia.

—CNBC's Jenny Lee contributed to this report.

title: OpenAI 首席财务官 Sarah Friar 告诉员工，7 月份的年化收入超过第二季度所有收入
content:
随着 OpenAI 在企业中追赶竞争对手 Anthropic，并试图在面对来自更便宜的开源替代方案的新竞争时保持增长，这家人工智能公司正在寻求让员工放心，业务保持健康。

据 CNBC 获悉，在周三与员工举行的内部会议上，财务总监莎拉·弗里亚尔 (Sarah Friar) 和董事会主席布雷特·泰勒 (Bret Taylor) 称赞了 OpenAI 的收入增长，并谈到了与 Anthropic 的竞争问题。 Friar 表示，OpenAI 7 月份的年化经常性收入超过了整个第二季度。

根据 CNBC 审阅的部分会议记录，Friar 表示，“第二季度也毫不逊色”。

Friar 和 Taylor 表示，这一势头是由该公司 GPT-5.6 系列模型的发布、名为 ChatGPT Work 的新企业代理以及越来越多地采用其 AI 编码工具推动的。 Codex。

OpenAI 面临着证明其 8520 亿美元估值合理性的压力，因为它正在为潜在的大规模 IPO 做准备。该公司面临着不断变化的竞争格局，其中包括 Anthropic 和 Google，以及大量来自中国的所谓开放权重模型，这些模型可以以更低的成本获得。本月早些时候，中国的 Moonshot AI 推出了 Kimi K3，该产品声称它缩小了与美国领先产品的差距，并在某些基准测试中超越了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 最强大的系统。

OpenAI 一直在竞相引入新用户，特别是企业和开发者，以产生帮助支持其基础设施支出计划所需的收入，该计划由外部资本资助。

2 月份，OpenAI 告诉投资者，它计划以到 2030 年，计算总支出约为 6000 亿美元。正如 CNBC 本周早些时候报道的那样，该公司目前正在与 Nvidia 讨论高达 2500 亿美元的支持，以资助其在俄亥俄州租用一个大型新 AI 数据中心的计划。

今年早些时候估值超过 OpenAI 的惊人数字和 Anthropic 的迅速崛起，引发了人们对 OpenAI 业务持久性的质疑。 Anthropic 在 5 月份表示，由于其 Claude Code 工具在开发者中大受欢迎，其运行率收入突破了 470 亿美元，高于 2025 年全年的约 100 亿美元。

The Information 在 3 月份援引一位知情人士的话说，OpenAI 最近的年化收入突破了 250 亿美元。

Taylor 周三告诉员工，Anthropic 的开局良好。今年，他承认 OpenAI 必须在编码市场上迎头赶上。但他说 Codex 的增长让他深受鼓舞。

泰勒在会议上表示：“你会看到人们深入研究 Claude Code，最终得到了非常高的费用，并开始寻找替代方案。”

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都在 6 月份向美国证券交易委员会秘密申请了 IPO。两家公司都没有透露有关计划何时首次亮相的更多细节。

title: 预计英国央行将再次维持利率不变
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者：Kevin Peachey生活费用通讯员43分钟前发布英国央行政策制定者预计英国利率将第五次维持在3.75%。全球政治和经济前景的不确定性以及对价格的影响，意味着该行可能会继续对利率采取谨慎态度。其货币政策委员会（MPC）每年举行八次会议，其决定在很大程度上影响借款人的收费金额贷款和抵押贷款以及储户可获得的回报。基准银行利率处于 2023 年 2 月以来的最低水平，但很少有分析师预测任何短期变化。由五名女性和四名男性组成的委员会将于英国夏令时 12:00 宣布最新利率决定，维持普遍预期。银行利率是货币政策委员会将物价上涨率（通胀率）维持在 2% 目标的主要工具。最新官方数据显示，英国通胀率为截至6月的全年通胀率为2.6%，较上月略有下降，但仍高于2.3%的目标。7月通胀率可能会上升，因为苏格兰、英格兰和威尔士的数百万家庭感受到国内能源价格上涨13%的影响。通胀率上涨是伊朗战争对能源批发价格影响的结果。海湾冲突以及持久休战可能性的不确定性，笼罩着货币政策委员会本月和未来几个月的会议和决定许多分析师预计，在可预见的未来，利率将保持不变，下一次变化的可能性是加息。储蓄平台Flagstone的凯蒂·霍恩(Katie Horne)表示：“新政府站稳脚跟，中东局势变得越来越不确定，这意味着维持基本利率决定将是一剂值得欢迎的稳定剂。”对借款人和储户的影响 保留意味着跟踪抵押贷款利率的房主每月还款额将保持不变。然而，超过十分之八的抵押贷款客户有固定利率交易，而且英国主要贷方最近几天一直在提高新交易的利率。此类抵押贷款的利率直到交易到期（通常是两年或五年后）才会发生变化，然后选择新的抵押贷款来取代它。新的两年期固定交易的平均利率为根据金融信息服务 Moneyfacts 的数据，利率为 5.62%，为一个多月以来的最高水平。利率上升的原因是中东地区再次出现波动，导致贷款人的融资成本上升。个别公司不希望被大量申请淹没，因此该行业往往会集体行动。抵押贷款经纪人 L&C 的 David Hollingworth 表示：“持有贷款仍然受欢迎，但市场预期需要放松，我们才能期待贷款机构降息。”英格兰银行最近的预测表明，到 2028 年底，超过 500 万房主的每月抵押贷款还款额将增加。我的抵押贷款还款额可能会变化多少？按照这个利率，你的还款额可能会发生变化……每月变化为每月总额您提供的有关每月还款额的信息不足以在给定的年份内还清您的抵押贷款。此计算器不构成财务建议。它基于标准抵押贷款还款公式，该公式取决于抵押贷款规模和期限以及固定利率。它仅供参考，并不代表抵押贷款优惠对用户的适用性、资格或可用性。如需确切数字，用户需要联系官方抵押贷款机构。利率根据英格兰银行的基准利率和市场状况而波动。其他贷款受到货币政策委员会决定的影响，这也对储户可获得的回报产生关键影响。更高的银行利率或增加的可能性可以提高储户获得的利率。愿意将储蓄锁定在固定期限内的人可以获得的一些交易处于近两年来的最高水平。顶级一年期债券支付的保证利息为 4.91%，是自 2024 年 10 月以来新客户的最高利率。 Moneyfacts.相关主题个人理财货币生活成本货币政策委员会 (MPC)英格兰银行储蓄抵押贷款

title: 随着人工智能支出计划的挫败感加剧，Meta 股价下跌
content: 图片来源，路透社 图片说明，Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 已将公司转变为人工智能领域的大手笔。作者：Kali HaysTechnology 记者 发布时间：2026 年 7 月 29 日，英国夏令时间 22:29 更新时间：1 小时前 Meta 股价周三暴跌，原因是投资者对其在利润下降的情况下继续在人工智能 (AI) 项目上投入的承诺犹豫不决。Instagram 和 Facebook 背后的公司股价在公布 2026 年 7 月 29 日的业绩后下跌 11% 4 月至 6 月的季度数据显示，收入同比增长 28%，达到 610 亿美元（约合 456 亿英镑），而利润下降 14%，至 60 亿美元。Meta 表示，今年将支出 1300 亿美元至 1450 亿美元，主要用于人工智能项目，而三个月前计划支出 1250 亿美元。首席执行官马克扎克伯格表示，该公司的人工智能支出正在“加速我们核心业务的各个部分”，并计划开始Meta 的首席财务官 Susan Li 告诉金融分析师，将其技术出售给其他公司将有助于其提高人工智能支出的回报。“到 2028 年，我们将翻出很多底牌，”她说。此类业务尚未实现。根据其财务记录，Meta 本季度的自由现金流（支付运营费用后保留的现金流量）为 7.84 亿美元，这是该公司至少五年来公布的最低水平。Forrester 分析师 Mike Proulx 表示，“本季度它产生的现金几乎全部被人工智能基础设施支出吃掉了”。 “投资者现在必须决定 Meta 不断增加的人工智能计划清单是否代表公司多元化或分散注意力。”Proulx 补充道，“与 Meta 的 Metaverse 失误有一点相似之处，Meta 的支出再次超过了已证实的产品需求。”他指的是 Meta 之前在虚拟体验上花费的数百亿美元，但用户的满意度却持平。谷歌上周还报告了有史以来最低的剩余现金数额，这导致其股价暴跌。整个行业都下了大赌注，”扎克伯格在谈到人工智能支出时说道。 “我个人认为，随着时间的推移，投资于此的人们会感觉非常好，并会得到回报。”他在电话会议上表示，Meta 的人工智能能力和模型正在推动 Instagram 和 Facebook 的参与度，并提高小型企业制作广告的能力。扎克伯格补充说，该公司正在开发人工智能代理，或者说在某种程度上自主行动的人工智能聊天机器人。扎克伯格说，此类代理“将成为我们未来几个月和几年内产品线的下一波浪潮”。扎克伯格在电话会议中补充道，“很快，我们将拥有可以代表您 24/7 工作的代理”。 “优秀的个人代理需要开箱即用。我对此感到非常兴奋，我们很快就会有更多的东西可以分享。”他补充道，“我们是世界上最好的公司，能够为数十亿人提供体验。”至于 Meta 计划首次向其他公司出售人工智能模型和计算机工具，扎克伯格表示，第一步是使其 Muse Spark AI 模型“更容易让公司集成”。“我们希望为大企业建立一个大型业务，”扎克伯格说。 “我们的路线图上有更多的编码和产品工具。”尽管扎克伯格表示，此举将展示“与我们历史上不同的力量”，但他表示，财务机会太大，不容忽视。“这不仅仅是销售计算；它是 API 服务和生产力服务，我认为那里有一个非常非常大的机会，我们非常关注这一点。” 微软周三还公布了季度和全年业绩，它逆势而上，科技股下跌，股价上涨。盘后交易中涨幅为 5%。华尔街的积极反应表明，即使是巨额人工智能支出，如果不始终加上缺乏明确的财务回报，投资者也可以接受。从 4 月到 6 月的三个月，微软的销售额增长了 18%，达到 900 亿美元，利润增长 31%，达到 360 亿美元。微软也是 OpenAI 最大的投资者之一，首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 在与分析师的电话会议中解决了这家人工智能公司最近的问题。纳德拉表示：“你从中得到的最大的好处是你不能依赖任何一种模型。”微软首席财务官艾米·胡德表示，其明年全年的资本支出将达到 1750 亿美元，主要与人工智能和人工智能基础设施有关。这比截至 6 月份的一年中花费的 1900 亿美元还要少。相关话题元马克·扎克伯格人工智能InstagramWhatsAppFacebook

title: 杰弗里·冈拉克表示，债券市场正在告诉沃什，美联储必须开始对通胀采取行动
content:
DoubleLine Capital首席执行官杰弗里·冈拉克(Jeffrey Gundlach)表示，美国国债市场正在发出信号，如果政策制定者认真考虑实现2%的通胀目标，美联储需要做的不仅仅是强硬言论。

“如果你真的想达到2%，我认为你必须提高利率，”周三美联储做出最新政策决定后，冈拉克在CNBC的“收盘钟”节目中表示。 “我认为达到 2% 需要很长时间。我们可能在未来几年内无法实现这一目标。”

美联储将基准利率维持在 3.5% 至 3.75% 的范围内不变，这是人们普遍预期的决定。然而，这一举措并未获得一致批准，三位政策成员反对加息四分之一个百分点。

冈拉克表示，声明公布后，国债曲线上的不同走势表明投资者对美联储最终会跟进的怀疑。

“两年期国债今天上涨，因为它认为美联储在慢慢来，”他说。 “新闻发布会后，长期债券收益率大幅上升，因为债券市场维护者说，‘如果你真的想让我们相信你的说辞，你就必须开始行动。’”

基准10年期国债收益率上涨超过7个基点至4.681%，而30年期国债收益率飙升至5.213%，创2007年以来最高水平。两年期国债收益率下跌3个基点至4.244%。

长期端普遍与通胀和赤字预期挂钩，而短期端则与短期利率预期密切相关。

美联储主席凯文·沃什强调，美联储将采取必要措施实现2%的通胀目标。

“我理解本委员会滚动预测和评论的愿望，但就我们而言，我们需要观察市场反应直接且未经过滤的发展，”沃什说。 “当然，我想强调的是，该委员会的决定非常重要，在必要和适当的情况下，我们将毫不犹豫地采取行动。”

title: 中国机器人大军改变英国零售业
content: Image source,Geek+Image caption,Two thousand Geek+ robots are deployed across 10 sites in the UKBySuranjana TewariAsia Business Correspondent,ÂReporting fromHefei, ChinaPublished1 hour agoEvery time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Geek+ is developing humanoid robots for picking and packingThe UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites."Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount.""We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.In its response to the government's consultation on a new AI and innovation strategy, it urged ministers to ensure workers are involved in decisions about automation and that employers invest in retraining."Working with technologists, workers and unions can help steer the UK's research and innovation towards workers' priorities for automation... avoiding job-cutting, low-productivity automation," the TUC said in its report.Image source,Geek+Image caption,Geek+ robots can move pallets and entire shelves around warehousesHow China became a robotics leaderRobotics has become a strategic priority for Beijing under President Xi Jinping's drive to develop what he calls "new quality productive forces".With China's working-age population shrinking, policymakers increasingly see automation as essential to boosting productivity and maintaining the country's manufacturing advantage."The robotics story builds directly on China's electric vehicle ecosystem," says Kyle Chan, a researcher at the Brookings Institution.Batteries, electric motors, cameras, sensors and semiconductors developed for electric vehicles (EVs) are increasingly being used across China's robotics sector, creating what he describes as "overlapping industrial ecosystems".One company leading that crossover is Chinese EV maker XPeng, which unveiled its humanoid robot, Iron, last year.Founder He Xiaopeng says he no longer sees XPeng simply as a carmaker."We want XPeng to be a high-tech company," he told the BBC. "In the future, any car company will transform into a car and robotics company."Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Leading EV maker XPeng is now developing humanoid robotsAnalysts say China's robotics push could follow a similar path as its global EV success, with local players using manufacturing prowess, dense supplier networks and rapid product development to establish an early lead."China is deliberately trying to build on some of those strengths," says Chan. "As it reaches into new areas, from humanoid robots to industrial robots to delivery robots."Tesla is pursuing a similar vision with its Optimus robot, which Elon Musk has said could eventually become a bigger business than carmaking.But China's ambitions to dominate the global robotics industry was dealt a blow this week whenthe US banned the import of new foreign-made advanced robots, citing national security.The Chinese embassy in Washington responded to the move by saying that Beijing has long opposed the US' "politicising" of trade issues and sanctions based on "groundless pretexts".The next frontierThe Chinese-made robots now operating in British warehouses are designed to solve the problem of moving goods. Geek+ says the company's next goal is to automate everything else."We are working on... end-to-end unmanned warehouse solutions," says Yanyu Liu, head of communications at Geek+.That means automating picking, handling and eventually packing goods.Across China, companies including AgiBot and Unitree are investing billions in humanoid robots.Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,AgiBot is developing humanoids for tasks carried out by humans in factoriesBut the business case for humanoids is less clear than it is for today's warehouse robots. If wheeled robots move goods cheaply, reliably and efficiently or robots with just arms can do the other automated tasks, what problem does a humanoid solve?Developers say factories, hospitals and offices have all been designed around people, and so they may eventually be able to work in different environments without the need to redesign workplaces around automation.But experts and developers alike agree that the current technology is not yet suitable for some repetitive tasks that require more dexterity."I don't think [humanoids] will change the landscape of the types of technology or the automation that's going to be put into place," says Pemberton. "They're definitely going to be complementary."Chinese companies already account for the vast majority of global humanoid deployments, but it may be years before they are commonplace in warehouses.For Britain, where productivity pressures and labour shortages are driving demand for automation, the country's warehouses are becoming an early testing ground for China's next major technology export.Additional reporting by Jaltson Akkanath ChummarRelated topicsInternational BusinessChinaRobotics

title: 以下是道琼斯指数最近一次下跌 1,000 点的情况以及接下来发生的情况
content:
在美联储决定维持利率稳定而美国油价接近每桶 85 美元后，道琼斯工业平均指数周三下跌超过 1,000 点。

在过去五年中，该蓝筹股指数已九次收盘跌幅超过 1,000 点。通常情况下，该指数往往会在大幅下跌后的一周内下跌，但随后在接下来的一个月和三个月内表现良好。

道琼斯指数在单日下跌 1,000 点后，每天中位数持平。一周后，其业绩恶化，下跌1.14%。然而一个月后，道琼斯指数的中值涨幅接近 2%。三个月后，这一涨幅飙升至 9.1%。

9 次 1,000 点下跌中有 3 次发生在唐纳德·特朗普总统 2025 年 4 月的“解放日”之后的余波中，当时他宣布对全球各国全面征收互惠关税。特朗普宣布暂停关税计划 90 天后，道琼斯指数和大盘在最初两天的大幅下跌后出现反弹，但由于对中国的高关税仍然存在，蓝筹股平均线在 4 月 10 日再次下跌。

美国在特朗普和中国发出贸易紧张局势缓和的信号后，股市于 4 月晚些时候开始复苏。

2022 年还发生了四次下跌。那年通胀飙升，美联储多次上调隔夜利率以遏制通胀。投资者担心利率上升可能导致经济放缓并可能导致经济衰退，从而推动道琼斯指数和其他主要股指跌入熊市区域。

市场于 2022 年 10 月触底，当前牛市开始。

道琼斯指数的另外两次大幅下跌发生在 2024 年 8 月和 12 月。前者是由于就业报告弱于预期和美国就业报告疲软后对美国劳动力市场的担忧推动的。

当前，投资者对美联储在通胀高于目标的情况下在2026年7月会议结束时保持观望的决定感到担忧。在特朗普承诺打击伊朗以报复对美军的突然袭击后，油价再次上涨。尽管央行决定暂时将利率维持在 3.5% 至 3.75% 的当前区间，但三名成员反对加息，这表明利率可能即将上升。

从历史来看，这一单日下跌的影响可能会进一步持续。

——CNBC 的 Fred Imbert 贡献了报道

title: 咖啡巨头上调全年展望，星巴克股价上涨
content:
Starbuckson Wednesday raised its full-year outlook after reporting its fourth straight quarter of same-store sales growth.

For fiscal 2026, Starbucks now expects adjusted earnings per share in a range of $2.55 to $2.65, up from its prior outlook of $2.25 to $2.45 per share.

It now also projects global same-store sales will rise nearly 6% and U.S. same-store sales will climb more than 6%; the company was previously forecasting global and U.S. same-store sales growth of at least 5%.

"This was the quarter our momentum became truly measurable," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared with the company's earnings press release.

The coffee giant also reported quarterly earnings and revenue that topped analysts' expectations.

Shares of the company jumped as much as 9% in extended trading.

Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended June 28 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

The coffee giant reported fiscal third-quarter net income attributable to Starbucks of $1.05 billion, or 91 cents per share, up from $558.3 million, or 49 cents per share, a year earlier.

The company's operating margins expanded to 13.6%, up from the year-ago period margins of 13.3%, thanks in part totariff refunds. Starbucks did not say exactly how much it received in refunds.

"The refunds we received in Q3 largely offset related tariffs incurred in the first three quarters of fiscal 2026," CFO Cathy Smith said on the company's earnings conference call.

Excluding restructuring costs and other items, Starbucks earned 85 cents per share.

Net sales dropped 1% to $9.3 billion due to the company's sale of a controlling stake in its China business. In November, Starbucks announced it was forming a joint venture with Boyu Capital, which would take over operations in the coffee chain's second-largest market.

Although Starbucks' overall revenue fell, its sales at stores open at least 13 months climbed 7.9%, topping Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount.

The coffee chain reported increases in both transactions and average check, showing that customers are returning to its cafes and spending more on their orders.

Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service and making cafes more welcoming in its home market. To do so, the chain has invested in labor and renovations to its coffee houses, earning somegrumbling from investors. But the efforts seem to be paying off for Starbucks, which had seen its sales slump as it lost many of its loyal customers to competitors likeDutch Bros.

The company's North American same-store sales increased 8.1% in the quarter. Traffic to those restaurants jumped 4.5%. With a 3.5% increase in average ticket, customers were also spending more on their orders, paying to modify their lattes and adding food items alongside their drinks.

In addition to improving its operations, Starbucks has also retooled its menu, cutting unpopular items and launching new drinks. Niccol said the chain would test "spritzers" — sparkling versions of its Refreshers — in select markets.

Refreshers have grown to become a $2 billion drink platform for Starbucks and often drive customers to its cafes during the afternoon, helping fuel business outside of the morning coffee rush. In the fiscal third quarter, revenue from Refreshers climbed by a double-digit percentage, executives said.

Outside of Starbucks' home market, same-store sales rose 5.7%. With the formation of the China joint venture, roughly 90% of the company's international locations are now licensed, according to Niccol. The asset-light model is often more attractive to investors, who like the long-term lift to earnings the structure usually brings.

During the quarter, Starbucks opened 175 net new stores and surpassed1,000 cafe "uplifts,"reaching its fiscal 2026 goal ahead of schedule. Starbucks is now targeting at least 1,500 store renovations by the end of fiscal 2026 and accelerating its plans further in the next fiscal year.

The cafe makeovers cost roughly $150,000 on average and result in higher transactions, Niccol said on the company's earnings conference call. The changes vary based on location, but generally customers can expect more seating, warmer lighting and dark wood paneling.

Smith also said that the company is assessing its North American store footprint, which could result in it shuttering more stores. In fiscal 2025, the company's North America footprint shrank by 1% due to closures.

Correction: This story was updated to correct that Starbucks' North American same-store sales rose 8.1%. A previous version misstated the figure.

title: 美联储会议回顾：沃什称美联储将毫不犹豫地阻止通胀，但债券市场心存疑虑
content:
TheFederal Reservereleased its latest interest rate decision on Wednesday, opting to keep rates at a range of 3.5% to 3.75%.

Though markets largely expected the Federal Open Market Committee to stay on hold, recent talk from several officials indicate there's a sizable constituency to at least consider a hike.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan was most specific, saying she thinks rates should be"modestly" higher, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis and Governor Christopher Waller all have made statements supportive of tighter policy should inflation persist.

Indeed, those three policymakers dissented with the Fed's decision.

At the post-decision press conference, Fed ChairmanKevin Warshsaid that while the Fed won't provide hints on where rate policy is heading, it will take necessary steps to meet its 2% inflation goal.

"I understand the desire for rolling forecasts and commentary from this committee, but for our part, we need to observe market reaction to developments direct and unfiltered," he said. "I want to stress, of course, that decisions by this committee matter a great deal, and where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act."

Bond yields jumped following the meeting, with the30-year Treasury yieldtopping 5.2% and hitting its highest level since 2007. The rate on the 10-year yield rose more than 7 basis points to 4.677%.

Inflation numbers of late have been at least a little comforting, as a brief decline in gasoline saw theconsumer price indexpost a surprise 0.4% drop in June. But the price break at the pump has been reversed in the past few weeks as the situation in the Middle East has been highly volatile.

"We're going to have an interesting set of data points come out between now and the September meeting," said Jerry Templeman, a former senior analyst at the New York Fed and now vice president of economics and fixed income research at Mutual of America Capital Management. "So, I don't think that we're going to necessarily be in the same position that we are today."

President Donald Trump appeared to claim that Warsh would like to lower interest rates, but he's being held back by the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee.

"Kevin's fantastic, but he's got a board," Trump, a long-time advocate for slashing rates, said at the White House when asked if he was at all disappointed with the Fed's decision to keep them unchanged.

"I know he'd love to see lower interest rates, but he's got a board, and it's a political board, and they want to keep rates up," Trump said.

"But we fight through rates," the president added.

The labor market has taken a backseat to inflation in the Fed's eyes, according to Aubrey Woessner, economist at the Indeed Hiring Lab.

"Amidst all the ambiguity, one thing is clear: the trajectory of prices, not the labor market, will determine which policy scenario prevails in the short run," Woessner said. "For now, the labor market is playing second fiddle, while inflation has first chair."

Woessner noted that the labor market appears "more stable" compared with several months earlier.

The major averages were heading for a losing day after Fed Chair Warsh wrapped up his July press conference.

The S&P 500 was down 0.6% at 3:24 p.m. ET, while the Nasdaq Composite was off 0.5%. The Dow Industrials were last down more than 840 points, or 1.6%.

The rate on the 10-year Treasury yield rose 5 basis points to 4.657%, but the 2-year yield slid 4 basis points to 4.236%. The 30-year Treasury bond yield advanced more than 9 basis points to 5.193%.

Warsh confirmed that post-decision press conferences will continue in 2026.

"Between now and year end, my predecessors and the Federal Reserve committed to press conferences this year. I'm committing to press conferences this year," he said at the conference Wednesday.

Warsh has stressed changing the way the Fed communicates, even dedicating one of five task forces he has created to address the issue.

With no meeting in August, the next big challenge for Warsh will be the Fed's annual policy retreat in Jackson Hole, Wyo. The event will run from Aug. 27 to 29.

Traditionally, Fed leaders have used the symposium to outline broad policy objectives. Warsh said his keynote speech, for now, is "a blank piece of paper right now."

However, he did say that he will be meeting with leaders of the five policy task forces he has created, and could use whatever information he gleans there as a starting point for the speech.

"In the next couple weeks, I'm going to be doing a check back in, giving them time to sort of think hard about their agenda, their debate, their schedule, and when they might be ready for prime time," he said. "I'll be doing a little bit of that checking, and that may or may not inform anything I have to say in Jackson."

When asked by a reporter about the argument to "pause" interest rates rather than hike or cut them, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said he wouldn't characterize the decision that way.

"I wouldn't characterize what we did as anything like a pause. I would characterize what we did as a rigorous review of the economic situation," he said. "I would characterize what we did as a review of the big hard questions, and I'd characterize it as a view of what our own homework is to try to resolve those questions in the period ahead."

He added that while the central bank decided not to alter interest rates today, this is merely the beginning of a story, not the end.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh across five public appearances hasused the phrase "family fight" 13 times, and he used it again to acknowledge the three dissents over the central bank's July interest rate decision.

"I asked for a good family fight, and I got one," he said. "Most of our discussion were on the big questions that matter to the conduct of monetary policy. We we didn't sort of hide from them. We weren't scared of them. There was a lot more interaction between and among my colleagues. It was a real family fight."

While the majority of members of the Federal Open Market Committee agreed with holding rates steady in July, three dissented, arguing instead to hike rates to combat above-target inflation.

While the Fed held rates steady, the three dissents in the committee resulted in an "uncomfortable hold," according to Christian Hoffmann, head of fixed income at Thornburg Investment Management.

"I'm calling this an uncomfortable hold," Hoffmann said.

Hoffmann noted that the decision follows some "constructive" inflation readings. But he noted that oil is again rising as the conflict between the U.S. and Iran heats up once more.

Vanguard's senior economist, Adam Schickling, expects a prolonged period of policy stability.

"While inflation remains elevated, we believe a cooling labor market and the limited effectiveness of monetary policy against supply-driven inflation pressures will make ... rate hikes difficult this year," he said. "The most important uncertainty facing markets today isn't Fed messaging—it's the combination of geopolitical risks and the long-term economic impact of AI."

While the Fed again chose not to act at this meeting, Warsh pledged that the central bank will take action if needed on inflation.

The central bank chairman also noted, however, that the Fed under his watch isn't in the forecasting business and won't be providing further hints about where rates are heading.

"I understand the desire for rolling forecasts and commentary from this committee, but for our part, we need to observe market reaction to developments direct and unfiltered," he said. "I want to stress, of course, that decisions by this committee matter a great deal, and where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act."

Federal Reserve Chairman Warsh acknowledged that treasury yields have risen since the last meeting of the central bank, despite the decision to hold rates steady today. That's a fact that he welcomes.

"Market attention centered on real data and real economic developments. Prices reacted in real time to incoming information," he said. "Market participants are learning to play the ball, not the referee, and market prices will continue to respond in the direction and magnitude they see fit."

Warsh added that trend is one for the better, saying the Fed doesn't always need to be the center of attention.

Earlier in his press conference, Warsh reiterate a key goal of the Fed is to keep inflation at manageable levels.

"You've heard this before, but we will deliver price stability," Warsh said.

Warsh said the Fed does not have soft targets for inflation. He said the one target they are working towards is the 2% annual rate deemed healthy for the economy.

"We have begun a new chapter, and we understand that the five-plus years of inflation above target cannot be cured in nine weeks, or by a single month of modest price decreases," Warsh said. "This Fed will not waver. Our credibility rests on performing our duties and delivering on our responsibilities."

While the Federal Open Markets Committee opted to keep rates steady, a trio of policymakers dissented in favor of a hike – the most seen since September 2016.

The "no" votes in July's meeting came from regional presidents: Beth Hammack of Cleveland, Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis andLorie Logan of Dallas.

title: 芯片制造商发布少量盈利指引，高通将在内存紧缩期间提高价格
content:
高通公司周三公布的第三财季收益符合分析师预期，但它对本季度收益提供了少量的内线收入指引，并将其归咎于计算机零部件（尤其是内存）持续的供应紧缩。

首席执行官克里斯蒂亚诺·阿蒙（Cristiano Amon）在接受采访时表示，高通公司正在采取具体措施扩大未来的利润率，包括从 9 月 1 日开始全面提高该公司芯片的价格，其中大部分是芯片产品的价格。目前正在转向智能手机制造商，并寻找其他方法来简化公司的供应链。

“成本上升，价格也会上涨，”阿蒙说。

这家芯片制造商的做法与 LSEG 的一致预期相比：

在本季度，高通表示预计调整后每股收益在 2.05 美元到 2.25 美元之间，营收在 97 亿美元到 10.5 美元之间亿。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计，调整后每股收益为 2.36 美元，销售额为 100.2 亿美元。

高通公司在其新闻稿中表示，“半导体行业的晶圆制造、组装、测试、先进封装、内存和其他材料的投入成本正在普遍增加”，但正如管理层指出的那样，“收入仍然保持健康。”

尽管如此，该公司的手机业务仍然是芯片销售的最大部分。阿蒙领导下的高通公司正在寻求多元化发展，涉足汽车、智能眼镜和机器人领域，并计划明年非智能手机销售额占公司收入的 60%。

高通公司公布的手机芯片销售额为 51 亿美元，同比下降 20%，该公司表示，这反映了中国市场的触底反弹。

阿蒙表示，智能手机市场的动态使得中低端手机芯片销售额下降由于负担能力问题，手机竞争力较差。他还表示，即使是高通占主导地位的高端 Android 手机，客户也在寻求更低的价格。

“由于内存价格上涨，高端类别的消费者偏好正在转变为对高端手机以及去年手机的偏好，”Amon 说道。

“由于你们都听说过的供应成本高昂，毛利率也发生了变化，”Amon 补充道。 “这是我们通过提价来解决的暂时性、短期问题。”

高通的汽车业务是一个亮点。高通公布的汽车销售额为 15.9 亿美元。该公司 6 月份表示，计划到 2029 年实现 100 亿美元的汽车收入。周三，该公司宣布与宝马达成数字驾驶舱芯片的芯片供应协议。

该公司还希望进军快速增长的人工智能数据中心基础设施市场。阿蒙表示，明年数据中心收入仍有望达到 50 亿美元。周三，高通还宣布完成了对Modular的收购，Modular是一家为人工智能提供编程技术的热门软件公司，该公司表示将在8月的一次会议上推出其人工智能软件平台。

该公司的低功耗工业用途芯片和智能眼镜被列为物联网收入。该部门的销售额同比增长 9%，达到 18.3 亿美元。

该季度净利润为 20 亿美元，比去年同期的 26.6 亿美元下降 25%。

高通通过其 QTL 部门获得了可观的利润，该部门将其蜂窝连接和其他芯片技术的知识产权许可给其他公司。高通的 QTL 收入为 12.8 亿美元，高于 StreetAccount 估计的 12.6 亿美元。

title: 托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 总检察长提名因科宁质疑特朗普与国税局和解而紧张
content:
周三，托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 的总检察长提名面临风险，因为一位重要的共和党参议员第二次取消了与布兰奇的会面，该会面旨在解决对唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统针对国税局 (IRS) 诉讼的有争议解决方案的担忧。

得克萨斯州参议员约翰·科尼尼 (John Cornynof) 表示，他取消了与代理总检察长布兰奇 (Blanche) 的会面，因为司法部没有满足他澄清法案条款的要求。和解协议使特朗普和其他人免受美国国税局对和解前提交的纳税申报表的审计。

科宁，布兰奇需要他的投票才能获得参议院司法委员会的提名，当被问及为什么司法部没有满足他的担忧时，科宁告诉记者“打败了我”。

“也许他们认为我会放弃，或者，你知道，继续，”据《MS NOW》报道，科宁说。 “但他们错了。”

科宁还表示，他相信司法委员会的另一位共和党人、北卡罗来纳州参议员托姆·蒂利斯“与我的观点基本一致。”

科宁说：“所以他们最好采取现实行动，而且时间不多了，”科宁说。

蒂利斯和科宁一样，对和解协议中的另一项条款（即设立 18 亿美元的基金）表示担忧。布兰奇是特朗普的前刑事辩护律师，他表示，在国会议员严厉批评该基金后，他取消了该基金，但蒂利斯、科宁和其他人要求提供书面保证，保证该基金无法恢复。

布兰奇的提名需要获得司法部门多数成员的支持，才能获得参议院全体投票。委员会定于周四进行投票。该委员会有 12 名共和党成员和 10 名民主党成员。预计每个民主党人都会投票反对布兰奇。

如果科宁或蒂利斯投票反对布兰奇，这将阻止他的提名进入参议院全体会议。

科宁说，司法委员会主席、爱荷华州共和党参议员查克·格拉斯利告诉他，他需要在下午 4 点之前知道。美国东部时间周三，小组对布兰奇提名的投票是否可以按计划在周四进行。

“所以，我们还有一点时间，希望他们现在认识到问题的严重性，”科宁说。

当被问及他是否会投票“不”将布兰奇的提名推进参议院全体会议时，科宁回答说：“嗯，我不准备投票‘同意’。”让我这么说吧。”

特朗普周三晚些时候告诉记者，他相信布兰奇的提名“进展顺利”。他还表示，他相信科宁对他感到不安，因为特朗普没有在德克萨斯州共和党初选中支持这位参议员，而州总检察长凯克斯帕克斯顿赢得了总统的支持。

科宁希望修改的和解协议解决了特朗普因代理承包商非法泄露其税务记录而对美国国税局提起的诉讼。

科宁希望司法部以书面形式保证布兰奇在他的确认听证会上就条款提供保证和解协议的内容，该协议保护特朗普、家庭成员和商业实体免受国税局审计以及与和解日期之前提交的纳税申报表相关的执法行动。

布兰奇作证说，该和解协议无意保护非诉讼当事人，也无意提供未来的税务审计豁免权，并且不适用于除国税局和财政部以外的任何政府机构。

“对我来说，这很简单。他们可以在修改后的文件中声明这一点。发布表格，这将回应我的要求，”科宁说。 “但出于某种原因，我不知道是否是司法部的工作人员或是谁，但他们只是……知道自己需要做什么，但他们只是拒绝这样做。”

一位司法部官员在向 CNBC 发表的一份声明中被问及科宁的说法时表示，“在与委员会和参议员办公室进行持续讨论后，司法部昨天向科宁参议员的工作人员提供了一份书面提案。”

“我们期待着”该官员表示，“以进一步讨论任何悬而未决的问题。”该官员表示。

科宁早些时候表示，“我还没有看到任何一篇文章能够满足我的要求。”

科宁在共和党初选中输给了帕克斯顿，将于 1 月离开参议院。蒂利斯将于 1 月份任期结束时从参议院退休，这使得两位参议员都可以在不担心赢得连任的情况下采取政治立场。

title: 萨姆·奥尔特曼将于本周在人工智能框架截止日期之前会见白宫的怀尔斯
content:
OpenAICEO萨姆·阿尔特曼周三告诉 CNBC，他已经看到了执行唐纳德·特朗普总统人工智能行政命令的拟议框架，并且他将于本周在华盛顿与白宫办公厅主任苏西·怀尔斯会面。

怀尔斯是特朗普最亲密的顾问之一，也是帮助制定政府人工智能政策方针的关键官员之一。奥尔特曼正在与特朗普的一系列高级官员会面。政府官员、立法者和经济学家本周将讨论 OpenAI 即将推出的模型、网络安全以及美国在全球人工智能竞赛中的地位。

自特朗普于 6 月份签署备受期待的行政命令以来，特朗普政府在人工智能监管方面发挥了更加积极的作用。该命令要求人工智能公司在全面发布之前自愿向政府提供模型，以评估其能力，但没有透露具体细节。

特朗普给联邦机构 60 天的时间来制定一个框架，以在实践中进行这些评估。

Altman 的华盛顿之行恰逢 8 月 1 日的最后期限即将到来，他并不是本周与立法者举行的唯一一位科技高管会议。Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 在国会大厦一位发言人告诉 CNBC，希尔将讨论开放模型和“美国在人工智能领域的领导地位”。

参议员。德克萨斯州共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹和几位参议院民主党人周三会见了奥尔特曼。 Altman 告诉 CNBC，他和 Cruz 讨论了“美国需要采取什么措施才能保持人工智能的竞争力。”

——CNBC 的艾米丽·威尔金斯 (Emily Wilkins) 和凯伦·斯隆 (Karen Sloan) 对本报告做出了贡献

title: 美国连续第五次维持利率不变
content: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社图片说明，美联储主席凯文·沃什撰文：Michael RaceBusiness 记者，纽约报道2026 年 7 月 29 日发布，英国夏令时间 19:02 44 分钟前更新美国利率已连续第五次被美联储维持不变。这一决定符合广泛预期，意味着利率将维持在 3.5% 至 3.75% 之间。利率越高，借贷越多对于那些想要获得贷款、抵押贷款和信用卡的人来说，利率昂贵，但可以带来更好的储蓄回报。政策制定者决定将利率维持在去年12月以来通胀后的水平，物价上涨的速度上个月放缓，但人们仍然担心下跌可能是短暂的。尽管截至6月的一年里通胀率降至3.5%，但利率上涨仍高于美联储2%的目标，五年多以来一直如此。上个月通胀率较低并不意味着价格正在下跌，而是价格上涨速度较慢。中东持续冲突对全球油价以及未来几个月一般消费者价格的影响也存在越来越大的不确定性。周三，全球油价基准布伦特原油上涨逾 6%，至每桶 89 美元以上。美联储承认通胀仍然“高位”，并称部分原因是能源价格上涨，但表示，尽管中东冲突造成不确定性，美国经济活动仍在“稳健”扩张。但美联储政策制定者以 9 比 3 投票赞成维持利率不变。三名投反对票的人转而推动小幅加息，猜测未来可能会进一步加息。由于美国和伊朗之间的新一轮敌对行动推高了全球石油和食品价格，美联储可能会决定加息。当被问及为什么美联储不加息时，沃什表示，尽管家庭和企业对高油价感到“不耐烦”，但他的董事会只就职了八周半。他在新闻发布会上表示，我想用魔杖来纠正你和其他人的错误。沃什表示，他曾希望并成功地与其他政策制定者就利率决定进行一场“家庭斗争”。“我要求进行一场良好的家庭斗争，我得到了。这就是目的。这就是设计特点，”他补充说，“我们在房间里做出的决定得到了绝大多数人的支持”。英国嘉信理财董事总经理理查德·弗林表示，对美联储来说，“最大的烟雾信号”是能源市场，伊朗持续的冲突可能会影响未来的利率决定。“我们预计，即使期货市场定价加息，美联储也将坚持到年底，”他说。沃什于五月由美国总统唐纳德·特朗普任命，自担任主席以来，他曾两次维持利率不变。他此前曾向国会表示，央行“无法容忍持续高涨的通胀”，并致力于“恢复物价稳定”。特朗普总统敦促沃什的前任杰罗姆·鲍威尔降息，并明确表示，他希望沃什满足降低美国人借贷成本的要求。但这位新任美联储主席表示，他的“目标”是“没有政治”，并强调了政策的重要性。美联储的独立性。 投资管理公司Quilter Cheviot固定利率研究主管理查德卡特表示，特朗普将饶有兴趣地关注美联储的决定，特别是距离美国中期选举还有不到100天的时间，“总统将希望传递有关经济的积极消息，”他补充道，“通胀继续保持高位，迫在眉睫的加息潜力肯定会让这种说法难以实现。” 提高利率是通过借贷来应对通胀的一种方式。价格上涨，鼓励人们削减支出，进而导致需求下降和物价上涨放缓。但这是一种平衡行为，因为高利率可能导致企业推迟投资，损害经济，同时，较低的利率可以通过降低借贷成本并鼓励支出和投资来提振经济。相关主题美联储通货膨胀美国经济。

title: 沃伦和希夫敦促美国证券交易委员会调查特朗普媒体的付费服务，以便更快地访问特朗普的帖子
content:
Sens。伊丽莎白·沃伦和亚当·希夫询问美国证券交易委员会调查特朗普媒体和科技集团是否通过出售更快地访问唐纳德·特朗普总统的真相社会帖子而违反了法律。

民主党参议员在周二给美国证券交易委员会主席保罗·阿特金斯的一封信中写道：“这似乎是为了个人利益而对总统办公室的粗暴滥用，损害了普通投资者和我们市场的诚信，同时让华尔街和其他富有的内部人士致富。”他们要求。阿特金斯将在 8 月 1 日开始之前完成对特朗普媒体新服务的法律分析，包括“禁止内幕交易和市场操纵”的法律。

特朗普媒体发言人在给 CNBC 的一份声明中予以反驳，指责参议院民主党人错误地描述了该服务，“要么是出于对自由市场的意识形态反对，要么是未能把握公开信息和非公开信息之间的区别，或者很可能两者兼而有之。”

美国证券交易委员会拒绝透露这一信息。对马萨诸塞州参议院银行委员会高级成员沃伦和参议院司法委员会成员加利福尼亚州希夫的信发表评论。

特朗普家族是这家上市公司的最大股东，该公司的股票代码为 TMTG，在纳斯达克交易的股票代码为 DJT（总统的姓名首字母缩写）。其股价曾被视为特朗普政治地位的晴雨表，自 2024 年 3 月下旬开始交易以来，其股价已下跌约 80%。

TMTG 运营着 Truth Social，这是迄今为止特朗普账户最受关注的社交媒体平台，该公司已涉足许多其他领域，包括加密货币和核聚变能源。

特朗普经常发布政策公告和其他有新闻价值的信息，包括有关伊朗战争的信息，这些信息导致全球市场急剧上涨或向下。他还多次使用自己的账户推销个股。

7 月 16 日，TMTG 宣布推出 Truth API，这是一项所谓的许可数据服务，提供“实时访问来自排名最高的 Truth Social 账户的帖子”。

该服务“提供平台上最具市场影响力的真理的直接、许可、实时反馈”，TMTG 的临时首席执行官 Kevin McGurn 表示。据路透社报道，TMTG 已讨论每月向该服务收取高达 10 万美元的费用。

在重新入主白宫之前，特朗普将超过 1.14 亿股 TMTG 股票转让给其家族管理的可撤销信托公司，但仍间接拥有这些股份。

沃伦和希夫写道，这项新服务“有可能破坏资本市场的诚信”。阿特金斯。

参议员们指出，特朗普“将从这项服务的推出中获利”，“支付订阅费的公司和富有的个人”也能更快地获得他的帖子。

他们警告说，Truth API 可以为高频交易公司提供特殊优势。 “虽然金融公司和分析师一直依赖对 Truth Social 的手动监控，但 API 会自动将全天候的 Truth Social 帖子直接直接提供给那些愿意预先支付毫秒级额外通知费用的人。”
